state_program_name: Home Health Agency license limited to non-skilled services (hands-on personal care by home health aides/CNAs; Ch. 400 Part III, F.S.; Rule 59A-8, F.A.C.) — or Homemaker and Companion Services registration (s. 400.509, F.S.) for companion-only care with no hands-on help; Nurse Registry as an independent-contractor alternative

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** ("the Agency") delivers non-skilled in-home care in the State of Florida in compliance with state and federal requirements. It applies to the Agency's chosen operating model:

- **Home Health Agency (HHA) license limited to non-skilled services.** Hands-on personal care is provided by home health aides/CNAs under Ch. 400, Part III, F.S. and Rule 59A-8, F.A.C.
- **Homemaker and Companion Services registration (s. 400.509, F.S.).** This applies to companion-only or homemaker-only care with **no hands-on help**.
- **Nurse Registry (s. 400.506, F.S.).** This is an alternative model in which referred caregivers are independent contractors and the registry may not supervise them. Use the nurse-registry provisions only if the Agency operates this way.

The manual is meant to:

1. Turn the governing statutes and rules into clear, repeatable procedures for administrators, supervising nurses, aides, companions, homemakers and office staff.
2. Protect clients by setting standards for client acceptance, service agreements, supervision, medication assistance limits, records, emergency planning and client rights.
3. Help the Agency show compliance during licensure and unannounced AHCA surveys.
4. Keep the Agency's licensed or registered scope of services consistent with what it advertises and actually provides.

**This manual is a template and must be customized.** Every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every bracketed item (names, addresses, license or registration numbers, counties served, administrator and alternate, RN supervisor, emergency coordinator and similar) must be completed. Any procedure that does not match the Agency's actual operations, licensure type or payer mix must be revised or removed before adoption. The manual does not replace the law and is not legal advice. If it conflicts with a statute or rule, the statute or rule controls.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize before use
- Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and bracketed field with Agency-specific information.
- Confirm which operating model applies: non-skilled HHA license, homemaker/companion registration, or nurse registry. Delete or mark as "not applicable" any policy that belongs to a different model.
- Mark the payer-specific sections (Medicaid SMMC, APD iBudget, Area Agency on Aging programs, EVV) as applicable or not applicable, depending on the contracts and enrollments the Agency actually holds.
- Complete the customization before the first client is served and before the manual is submitted with any application or survey.

### 2. Adoption by the governing body
- The owner, board of directors or other governing body of **[AGENCY NAME]** must formally review and adopt the manual. Record the adoption in the minutes or by signed resolution.
- Record the adoption date, the version number and the names of the approving individuals on the manual's cover or revision page: **[ADOPTION DATE]**, **[VERSION]**, **[APPROVED BY]**.
- The governing body must also formally adopt every material revision.

### 3. Keep it current
- Review the manual at least annually, and sooner when a statute, rule, form or payer requirement changes, when AHCA survey findings call for it, or when the Agency changes services, ownership, address, counties served or administrator.
- Check the current text of each cited rule and form against the official source before relying on it. Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C. (Personnel) is a particular case: the version effective 5/31/2026, as read on flrules.org, controls, and secondary websites may still show the prior version.
- Keep a revision log of changes, dates and approvers. Retain superseded versions according to the Agency's record-retention policy.
- Statutes and rules change. If the manual and the current law disagree, follow the law and update the manual promptly.

### 4. Train all staff
- Every employee (and every contractor where applicable) must be trained on the parts of the manual that apply to their role **before** they work independently, and again whenever the manual changes. Document the training with the date, content, trainer and the staff member's signature.
- Keep these documents in each personnel file. Training required by law is separate from, and in addition to, manual orientation. It includes:
  - the dementia-related training under s. 430.5025, F.S.;
  - the HHA aide training, competency and annual in-service requirements under Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C.;
  - the HIV/AIDS course;
  - CPR;
  - medication-assistance training, if applicable.
- Make the manual readily accessible to all staff, in print or electronically, and tell staff who to ask for clarification: **[COMPLIANCE CONTACT]**.

### 5. Organization and conventions
- Policies cite the controlling statute or rule so staff and surveyors can trace each requirement to its source. The full list is in the Regulatory Framework section below.
- Where a policy states a deadline, notice period or hour requirement, it comes from the cited authority. Do not shorten these in local procedures.
- Where the rules say the Agency "must have written policies" (for example, RN supervisor availability under Rule 59A-8.003(9)(d) and client notice delivery under s. 408.810(5)), the corresponding section of this manual serves as that written policy once adopted.

### 6. Use with forms and records
- Use the current official AHCA forms (such as Form 3110-1011 with Addendum, Form 3110-1003, Form 3110-1007 and Form 3110-1022) as cited in the regulatory framework. Confirm that each is the current edition before use.
- Keep client and personnel records as required by Rule 59A-8.022, F.A.C., Rule 59A-8.020, F.A.C., and s. 400.491, F.S. Records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator and Alternate Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Owners and governing body, administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor, and all management staff of [AGENCY NAME] (Home Health Agency limited to non-skilled services, or Homemaker and Companion Services registrant)
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, and to ensure that a qualified administrator and a qualified written on-site alternate administrator are always designated and accountable for day-to-day operations in compliance with Florida law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by its owner(s) or governing body, which is legally responsible for the agency's compliance with Chapter 400, Part III, F.S., and Rule 59A-8, F.A.C. The governing body appoints an administrator who meets the qualifications of s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S.: a Florida-licensed physician, physician assistant or registered nurse, or a person with at least one year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health care or in a facility licensed under Florida law. The administrator is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the agency. The agency also designates, in writing, an on-site alternate administrator who meets the same qualifications and who holds full authority whenever the administrator is absent. [AGENCY NAME] is a non-skilled agency and does not employ a director of nursing. An RN supervisor is still required for aide supervision, as described in SVC-04 and SVC-05. If skilled nursing services are ever added, the agency will first meet the additional requirements that apply to skilled agencies, including a director of nursing, before offering those services.

definitions.definition: The person who meets s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S., and who is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the agency.
A person who meets the administrator qualifications, is designated in writing, and has full authority to act for the administrator when the administrator is absent.
The owner(s), board, or other persons holding legal responsibility for the agency, [GOVERNING BODY NAME/DESCRIPTION].

A home health agency licensed only to provide services that do not require a nurse, such as hands-on personal care by home health aides and certified nursing assistants, and homemaker and companion services.
A provider registered under s. 400.509, F.S., to provide homemaker and companion services only, with no hands-on personal care.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written organizational chart showing the governing body, administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor, office staff, and aide/companion/homemaker staff. The administrator keeps the chart current and available to surveyors.

Before appointing an administrator, the governing body verifies and documents the qualifying credential: a Florida physician, PA or RN license verified on the Florida Department of Health license lookup, or at least one year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health or a licensed facility, supported by employer letters or verified employment history.
The governing body confirms that the administrator has completed Level 2 background screening before assuming the role (see PER-02) and files the screening result in the personnel file.
The governing body signs a written Administrator Appointment stating the administrator's name, start date, authority, and duties. A copy is kept in the governance file.

The administrator designates a written on-site alternate administrator who meets the same qualifications. The designation states the person's name, qualifications, effective date, and that the alternate holds full authority when the administrator is absent.

The alternate administrator must be a direct employee of [AGENCY NAME] or be provided through a management company or employee-leasing arrangement documented in a written agreement. The administrator keeps the agreement on file.

The alternate administrator is readily available on the premises or by telecommunications during business hours. The administrator posts a current contact sheet at the front desk with the phone numbers of the administrator and the alternate, and staff are trained to use it.

If the same person is proposed as alternate administrator for more than one home health agency, the administrator verifies before the designation that all of the agencies have identical controlling interests and are in the same service area or a contiguous county, and that no more than five agencies are involved. The administrator confirms the current rule text with AHCA in writing and keeps that confirmation on file.

The administrator carries out these duties: implementing and enforcing agency policies; ensuring that the RN supervisor is designated and available (SVC-04, SVC-05); ensuring that aides are qualified before they serve (PER-01, PER-03, PER-04); ensuring that records are kept (REC-01); and ensuring that required reports to the state are filed on time (REC-02).

The agency does not employ a director of nursing while it is non-skilled. Before adding any skilled nursing service, the administrator presents a written plan to the governing body covering the director of nursing, accreditation, on-call coverage, and license changes. No skilled service starts until AHCA has approved the change.

When the administrator or alternate administrator changes, the administrator notifies AHCA using the forms and process in Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C. The incoming person must complete Level 2 screening. The administrator files the notice and AHCA's acknowledgment in the governance file on the day it is sent or received.

Other changes to licensure information are reported to AHCA within 21 calendar days of the change. The administrator logs each change, the date reported, and the confirmation in the regulatory change log.

For the Homemaker and Companion Services registrant track (GOV-08), the agency names an administrator or managing employee and a financial officer on AHCA Form 3110-1003. One owner may fill both roles. Registrant staff are never assigned hands-on personal care.

The governing body meets at least [QUARTERLY/ANNUALLY] and keeps written minutes. Each meeting reviews QA results (GOV-04), complaints and incidents (CR-02, SAF-02), survey results, and any regulatory changes.

The governing body reviews the administrator's performance and the alternate administrator designation at least annually and whenever there is a change in staff. The review is documented in the minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints a qualified administrator and approves the alternate; holds legal responsibility for compliance; reviews QA results and regulatory changes.
Manages day-to-day operations; keeps the alternate designation current; reports changes to AHCA; ensures staff qualifications and record-keeping.
Holds full authority and acts for the administrator when absent; stays available on premises or by telecommunications during business hours.
Supervises aides and assigns personal care tasks as described in SVC-04; supports the administrator on clinical matters.
Use the contact sheet to reach the administrator or alternate; route calls and surveyor inquiries promptly.

documentation: Organizational chart with revision dates
Administrator qualification verification and Appointment document
Written alternate administrator designation and any management company or leasing agreement
Level 2 screening results for the administrator and alternate
AHCA notices of administrator or alternate change and acknowledgments
Regulatory change log
Governing body meeting minutes and annual reviews

policies.title: Licensure, Registration, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
policies.applies_to: Owners, administrator, alternate administrator, and any staff who prepare applications, advertising, websites, or marketing materials for [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure that [AGENCY NAME] holds the correct Florida license or registration for the services it provides, never serves clients before approval, advertises only services it is authorized to provide, and displays its license or registration number as required.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides only those services authorized by its AHCA license or registration. Any hands-on help requires a Home Health Agency license (which may be limited to non-skilled services) or a Nurse Registry license under Chapter 400, Part III, F.S. Hands-on help includes bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transfers, ambulation and medication assistance. Companion-only or homemaker-only care requires registration under s. 400.509, F.S. Under s. 400.462, F.S., companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care. [AGENCY NAME] does not accept or serve any client until the license or registration has been issued. Every advertisement shows the AHCA license or registration number. Advertising a service that is not on the license or registration is unlicensed activity under s. 400.464, F.S., and is prohibited.

definitions.definition: Hands-on assistance with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transfers and ambulation; requires a license (s. 400.462, F.S.).
Non-hands-on services such as companionship, light housekeeping, meal preparation and errands, provided by a registrant under s. 400.509, F.S.
A licensed referral service that refers independent contractors to clients, an alternative to the employee-based HHA model (s. 400.462, F.S.).
The county or counties that [AGENCY NAME] is authorized by AHCA to serve under its license.
Providing or advertising services that require a license or registration without holding one, or advertising services not authorized by the license held.

procedures: Before filing any application, the governing body decides in writing which track [AGENCY NAME] will use: (a) Home Health Agency limited to non-skilled services; (b) Nurse Registry; or (c) Homemaker and Companion Services registration. The decision is based on whether any hands-on personal care will be provided.

For the HHA track, the administrator submits the application on AHCA Form 3110-1011 with the Addendum, as required by Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C., and pays the fees listed on Form 3110-1011CL (a $1,705 license fee and a $300 assessment). Fees are nonrefundable.
The administrator includes with the HHA application proof of at least $250,000 per claim malpractice insurance and $250,000 per claim liability insurance (s. 400.471, F.S.).

The administrator obtains CPA-compiled two-year financial projections. The projections must show startup, working-capital and contingency funds covering at least three months of projected expenses, with a contingency of at least one month (s. 408.8065, F.S.), and must not project a 15 percent or higher operating margin in any month of year one.
The administrator obtains zoning approval for the office and evidence of the legal right to occupy the premises, and includes both with the application.
If any controlling interest is held by a nonimmigrant alien, the owner obtains and files the $500,000 surety bond required by s. 408.8065(2), F.S.
The agency understands that non-skilled HHAs are exempt from accreditation (s. 400.471, F.S.). The administrator confirms this status with AHCA at application and again if services change.

For the registrant track, the administrator submits AHCA Form 3110-1003 with the $50.75 biennial fee (Form 3110-1003CL) and the names of the administrator or managing employee and financial officer (see GOV-08).

The agency prepares for the licensure survey before initial licensure (s. 400.471(2) and Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C.). Policies, personnel files and records are completed and ready for review (see GOV-06).

The agency does not accept referrals, sign service agreements, or send staff to any client home until the license or registration is issued. The administrator records the issue date and license or registration number in the governance file.
The administrator keeps a calendar showing the license or registration expiration date and the renewal packet due date. Renewal is started at least [90] days before expiration.

The administrator reviews every advertisement, website page, social media profile, brochure and business card before publication. Each must show the AHCA license or registration number and must describe only services on the license or registration. The administrator initials and dates each approved item.

Registrant staff and materials never offer bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, medication assistance or any other hands-on care. If a registrant client needs hands-on care, the agency follows SVC-01 and refers the client to a licensed provider.

The agency serves only the counties authorized on its application. The administrator reads the current AHCA geographic service area rule before finalizing service-area wording in any application, ad or service agreement. Changes in counties served follow GOV-07.

If the agency learns that any ad or statement has described unlicensed services, the administrator removes it within one business day, records the correction, and reviews the cause at the next QA meeting. The administrator also reports any suspected violation of s. 400.464, F.S., to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Selects the license or registration track; funds the startup, working-capital and contingency requirements; carries insurance.
Prepares and files applications and renewals; approves all advertising; keeps the license or registration current and posted.
Use only approved materials; never describe services outside the license or registration; never schedule service before issuance.
Confirms that the services assigned to staff are within the scope of the license.

documentation: Track selection decision
Application packets (Form 3110-1011 and Addendum, or Form 3110-1003) with fee receipts
Insurance certificates, CPA projections, zoning approval, right-to-occupy evidence, and surety bond if applicable
Issued license or registration and renewal calendar
Advertising approval log with initials and dates
Corrections log for any ad found noncompliant

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor, and all staff who use or maintain the [AGENCY NAME] Policy & Procedure Manual
policies.purpose: To keep the Policy & Procedure Manual current with Florida law and AHCA rules, to ensure that only approved versions are in use, and to ensure that policies are ready for surveyor review at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a controlled Policy & Procedure Manual. Each policy has an owner, effective date, version number and approval signature. The manual is reviewed at least annually and whenever a statute, rule, form or AHCA guidance changes. Staff use only the current approved version. The administrator keeps the manual available for review during licensure surveys under Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C.

definitions.definition: The staff member responsible for keeping a policy accurate and current.
A record of each revision showing the date, version number, summary of change, and approver.
Any amendment to Chapter 400, Part III, F.S., Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C., or a related AHCA form or requirement that affects agency operations.

procedures: The administrator assigns each policy in the manual a policy owner and records the owner on the policy's cover page and in the version log.
Each policy carries its ID, title, version number, effective date, last review date, and the approval signature of the administrator and, for clinical policies, the RN supervisor.
The administrator reviews the full manual at least once every 12 months. The review is documented in the version log and the governing body minutes.

The administrator checks the Florida Administrative Register and the flrules.org text of Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C., and the Florida Senate statute site at least [QUARTERLY] for changes. Several rules in Chapter 59A-8 were amended in 2026, and a new AHCA rule titled 'Excellence in Home Health' takes effect October 12, 2026. The administrator reads the current official text of each and revises affected policies before the effective date.

When a regulatory change is found, the administrator logs it in the regulatory change log within 5 business days, identifies the affected policies, assigns owners, and sets a revision deadline no later than the effective date of the change.
The policy owner drafts the revision, marks it as a draft, and routes it to the administrator and RN supervisor for review. The administrator approves and dates the final version.

Within 5 business days of approval, the administrator issues the revised policy to all affected staff, records who received it, and obtains a signed acknowledgment for any change that affects job duties. Training under PER-03 is scheduled when procedures change.
The administrator removes superseded versions from active use and files them, marked 'Superseded' with the date, for at least [5] years or as long as the record-retention policy requires.

The administrator keeps a ready-to-review copy of the manual, in print or electronic form, at the office. In a survey, the administrator or alternate produces it on request. Surveyors will ask in particular for the policies on RN supervisor availability, hotline notice delivery, medication assistance and emergency management (see SVC-05, CR-07, SVC-06 and SAF-04).
After any survey deficiency, complaint finding, incident review or QA finding, the administrator considers whether a policy needs revision and records the decision in the QA file (GOV-04).
The administrator keeps the version log, regulatory change log, and staff acknowledgments in the governance file.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the manual; performs annual and regulatory-driven reviews; approves and issues revisions; keeps it available to surveyors.
Keep assigned policies accurate; draft revisions by assigned deadlines.
Reviews and approves clinical and supervision policies.
Use only current approved versions; sign acknowledgments; raise suspected policy gaps with the administrator.

documentation: Version log and policy cover pages with approval signatures
Regulatory change log
Staff acknowledgments of policy changes
Archive of superseded policies
Governing body minutes recording annual manual review

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor, and staff who maintain or review client records and operations at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To monitor the quality, safety and compliance of services through regular documented record review and data tracking, and to use the findings to improve care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a quality assurance (QA) program. Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C., requires a documented quarterly review of a sample of active and closed records by the director of nursing in skilled agencies. Because [AGENCY NAME] is non-skilled and has no director of nursing, the agency adopts this review as its own standard and assigns it to the RN supervisor or administrator. Results are reported to the governing body and used to improve services.

definitions.definition: A documented quarterly review of a sample of active and closed client records against the standards in this policy.
A measurable item tracked over time, such as supervisory visit timeliness or missed visits.
A documented step taken to fix a deficiency and prevent it from recurring.

procedures: The administrator appoints the RN supervisor (or the administrator) as QA reviewer and records the appointment in the governance file.

Each calendar quarter, the QA reviewer selects a sample of active and closed client records. The sample is at least [10 percent of records, minimum 5] and includes records of clients served by different aides and, if applicable, different payers.
The reviewer uses a written QA checklist to test each record against the required contents and standards in Rule 59A-8.022, F.A.C., and Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C. (see REC-01).
The reviewer confirms that clients accepted were within the agency's capability to serve (SVC-02).
The reviewer confirms that aide assignments were consistent with the plan of care and with the aide's training (SVC-03, SVC-04).
The reviewer confirms that services were documented, dated and signed, and that electronic signatures meet the authentication rules (REC-03).
The reviewer confirms that agency policies were followed, including written consent before the RN enters the home, medication-assistance consent and hotline notice delivery (CR-07, SVC-06).
The reviewer confirms that client confidentiality was maintained (CR-03).
In addition to record review, the reviewer tracks supervisory visit timeliness, missed visits, complaints, incidents, hotline reports, and client or family satisfaction comments each quarter.
The reviewer records findings, the specific records affected, and recommended corrective actions on the QA report within 30 days after the quarter ends.

The administrator assigns each corrective action to a named person with a due date, usually within 30 days, and verifies completion. Repeated findings trigger staff retraining (PER-03) or policy revision (GOV-03).
The administrator presents each quarterly QA report to the governing body at its next meeting. The minutes record the discussion and any decisions.
The administrator keeps QA reports and corrective-action records for at least [5] years and makes them available during surveys.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews QA reports; provides resources for corrective actions.
Oversees the QA program; assigns and verifies corrective actions.
Performs the quarterly record review and tracks performance indicators.
Cooperate with reviews; complete corrective actions assigned to them.

documentation: QA reviewer appointment
Quarterly QA checklists and reports
Indicator tracking logs (supervisory visit timeliness, missed visits, complaints, hotline reports)
Corrective-action plans and completion verification
Governing body minutes recording QA review

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, billing and scheduling staff, RN supervisor, aides, and all personnel of [AGENCY NAME] who create, review or submit records or claims
policies.purpose: To prevent fraud, waste and abuse; to ensure that [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered and documented; and to meet Florida and federal Medicaid provider requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for visits that were actually delivered, verified by electronic visit verification (EVV) where required and supported by signed service notes. No employee may falsify time, notes, signatures or claims. The agency discloses required history on applications, complies with Medicaid enrollment and screening requirements for providers serving managed care plans, and cooperates with audits by AHCA, Medicaid managed care plans and other payers. Violations result in discipline up to termination and, where required, reports to the appropriate authority.

definitions.definition: Knowingly submitting or causing a false claim or record, including billing for services not delivered.
Practices that result in unnecessary costs or improper payment, even without intent to defraud.
Electronic visit verification: an electronic record of the date, time, location, service and worker for a visit; required for Medicaid personal care and home health services (42 U.S.C. 1396b(l)).
A provider that serves members of a Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) plan under contract with the plan.

procedures: The administrator serves as compliance officer unless the governing body names another person. The compliance officer's name and contact information are given to all staff at orientation (PER-03).

Billing staff bill a visit only after matching three records: the schedule, the EVV record (SVC-09) or timekeeping record, and the signed service note. If any of the three is missing or conflicts, the visit is not billed until the discrepancy is resolved and the resolution is documented.

Staff may never bill for, or record time for, a visit that was shortened, missed, performed by another person, or provided outside the authorized plan of care. Missed or shortened visits are recorded as such (SVC-08).

Before any Medicaid or managed-care service starts, the administrator confirms that the service is authorized by the payer and that the agency holds the required Medicaid provider enrollment. Network providers serving SMMC plans must be screened and enrolled with Florida Medicaid (42 CFR 438.602). The administrator keeps the enrollment records on file.

The agency uses EVV for Medicaid personal care services and home health care services as federal law requires (42 U.S.C. 1396b(l)), following the payer's EVV system rules. Manual EVV edits require a written reason, are approved by the administrator, and are reviewed monthly.

Billing staff reconcile claims, payments and denials monthly. The administrator reviews all claim adjustments and any overpayment. Overpayments are reported to and returned to the payer within the payer's required time, and the return is documented.

On or before the first day of service, the agency gives each client the Medicaid fraud hotline notice and a written description of Medicaid fraud, along with the complaint and abuse hotline notices, as s. 408.810(5), F.S., requires. Delivery follows CR-07 and is documented in the client record.

The agency discloses on its applications any history of Medicare, Medicaid or CLIA exclusion or termination, as required by s. 408.810, F.S. The administrator reviews each owner's, controlling interest's and administrator's history before filing.

A controlling interest must notify AHCA within 10 days after a bankruptcy, foreclosure or eviction court action begins, and may not withhold evidence of financial instability (s. 408.810, F.S.). The administrator informs all owners of this duty. If such an action begins, the administrator files the notice and records it in the regulatory change log. Failure is a second-degree misdemeanor under the statute.

The administrator checks the Florida Medicaid and federal OIG exclusion lists for each owner, administrator and employee at hire and at least [MONTHLY/ANNUALLY]. Anyone found excluded is removed from billable work at once and the payer is notified as required.
At orientation and annually, all employees receive training on fraud, waste and abuse, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. 3729-3733), accurate documentation, EVV, and how to report concerns (PER-03).

Any employee who suspects fraud, falsified records or improper billing reports it to the compliance officer, or to the governing body if the concern involves the compliance officer. Reports may be made anonymously, and retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is prohibited.

The compliance officer investigates each report within [10] business days, documents the facts, takes corrective action, and, when required by law or contract, reports to AHCA, the managed care plan, the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, or other authority.
The agency cooperates with payer and AHCA audits and produces requested records within the deadline given. The administrator logs each audit, request, finding and response.
The compliance officer reports at least quarterly to the governing body on billing accuracy, EVV exceptions, audits, exclusion checks and reports received (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sets a culture of compliance; receives compliance reports; notifies AHCA of bankruptcy, foreclosure or eviction actions.
Runs the compliance program; approves manual EVV edits; investigates reports; handles audits and overpayments.
Match schedule, EVV and signed notes before billing; reconcile claims.
Verifies that services delivered match the plan of care; reports discrepancies.
Record time and services honestly; report suspected fraud.

documentation: Compliance officer designation
Billing reconciliation records and EVV exception logs
Medicaid enrollment and payer authorization records
Exclusion list check records
Training attendance records
Compliance report and investigation files
Audit log and overpayment return records
Hotline notice delivery records (see CR-07)

policies.title: Hours of Operation, Licensure Surveys and Surveyor Access
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor, front-office staff and all personnel of [AGENCY NAME] who may be present during an AHCA survey
policies.purpose: To ensure that [AGENCY NAME] is open and reachable to the public during required hours, and that surveyors can promptly obtain access to the administrator, records and client lists at any time, including during unannounced surveys.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps its office open and available to the public for any 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding legal and religious holidays, as required by Rule 59A-8.003(9), F.A.C. During those hours the administrator or alternate administrator is available. If neither is on the premises, a staff person answers the phone and the door and can reach them. When a surveyor arrives, the administrator, alternate, or another person authorized to give access to records is on the premises within one hour, and a list of current clients is produced within two hours if requested. [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully with all surveys.

definitions.definition: The 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, that the agency listed on its application, [BUSINESS HOURS], excluding legal and religious holidays.
An AHCA survey conducted without advance notice; occurs at least every 36.9 months after initial licensure.
A list of all clients currently receiving services, including the information the surveyor needs to select a sample.

procedures: The administrator sets the agency's 8 consecutive hours of public availability, [DAYS AND HOURS], between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The hours are the same as those listed on the application and are posted at the office entrance and on the agency's website and phone greeting.

The administrator or alternate administrator is available to the public during these hours. The rule describes the director of nursing for skilled agencies. Because [AGENCY NAME] is non-skilled, the agency names the administrator or alternate, and the RN supervisor will be available according to SVC-05. The administrator confirms with AHCA in writing how the RN role is applied to this requirement and keeps the response in the governance file.

If neither the administrator nor alternate is on the premises, a front-office staff person (clerical staff is acceptable) answers the phone and the door and can reach the administrator or alternate immediately. The front desk contact sheet lists current phone numbers for both.

The administrator confirms that the office is not closed during the posted hours. Being closed during those hours can lead to a fine or denial of a license. Planned closures for legal and religious holidays are posted in advance.

Before initial licensure, the administrator prepares for the survey by assembling policies, personnel files, training records, insurance, service agreements, sample client records, and the posted notices, so they can be reviewed in the office.

When a surveyor arrives, staff greet the surveyor courteously, ask for identification and the purpose of the visit, and immediately telephone the administrator and the alternate. No staff member refuses entry or delays access.

The administrator, alternate, or another person authorized to give record access arrives on the premises within one hour of the surveyor's arrival. The front-desk staff person records the surveyor's arrival time and the arrival time of the authorized person.

If the surveyor requests a list of current clients, the administrator or authorized staff member produces it within two hours of the request. The list is kept current weekly so it can be produced quickly.
The administrator makes client records, personnel files and policies retrievable during the survey, whether they are paper or electronic (REC-01, REC-03, REC-04).
A staff member accompanies the surveyor as needed, takes notes of requests and questions, and logs the documents provided. Staff answer questions truthfully and do not alter or back-date any record.
Client privacy is protected during record review. The agency provides access to AHCA surveyors as authorized by law and records what was disclosed (CR-03, REC-04).

At the exit conference, the administrator listens to preliminary findings and records them. The administrator obtains the written survey report, files it, and, if deficiencies are cited, prepares and submits the plan of correction by the deadline stated in the report.
The administrator keeps the survey report, the plan of correction, and evidence of corrections in the survey file, and reviews them at the next QA meeting and governing body meeting (GOV-04).
Follow-up surveys may occur at any time. The agency maintains compliance continuously and does not treat survey readiness as a one-time event.

The agency understands that failure to be available as required by the rule is grounds for denial or revocation of the license. The administrator reviews the hours posted, the contact sheet and the survey procedure with all front-office staff at hire and at least annually.

responsibilities.duty: Sets and posts business hours; ensures availability; leads survey response; submits any plan of correction.
Covers availability and survey duties when the administrator is absent.
Remains available per SVC-05; supports clinical record review during a survey.
Answer the phone and door; reach the administrator or alternate; log surveyor arrival; produce the client list when directed.
Reviews survey findings and ensures corrections are made.

documentation: Posted business hours and AHCA confirmation on RN role
Front-desk contact sheet
Surveyor arrival log (arrival times, persons notified, documents provided)
Weekly current client list
Survey reports, plans of correction and evidence of correction
Staff training records on survey procedure

policies.title: Satellite Offices, Drop-off Sites, Service-Area Changes and Change of Ownership
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Alternate Administrator, governing body, office staff. Applies to the Home Health Agency license (non-skilled). Registrant-specific timing is noted where it differs.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] opens, closes, moves or changes its offices, sites, counties served and ownership only in the way Florida allows, and that clients are never left without services or records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not open a satellite office, use a drop-off site, move its main office, add or remove counties, or change ownership until the Administrator has confirmed the AHCA filing requirement and the governing body has approved the change. A satellite office must be in the same geographic service area as the main office, share administration and supervision with it, and is not separately licensed. An office outside the service area requires its own license. A drop-off site is a work station only. All changes are filed with AHCA on the required form with the required evidence, and client records follow the client's care through any change of ownership.

definitions.definition: An additional office in the same geographic service area as the main office that shares its administration and supervision and is not separately licensed. The main-office Administrator is responsible for it.
A work station used by staff only. It has no contact with prospective clients, no billing, no housing of client records, and no display of the agency name at the location or in advertising.
A transfer of the agency to a new owner, which requires a new application to AHCA and transfer of all client records to the new owner.
The AHCA application form (paper or online version) used to report a change of address, counties served, or office opening or closing.

procedures: Before any change, the Administrator writes a one-page change proposal. It states the change (satellite, drop-off site, move, county change, closure or ownership transfer), the proposed date, the clients affected, and the effect on RN supervision and caregiver coverage. It is dated and filed in the governance binder.
The governing body reviews and approves or denies the proposal in writing at a meeting. The minutes are kept under GOV-01.
Satellite office: the Administrator confirms the location is in the same geographic service area as the main office. If it is not, no services are provided from it until a separate license is issued.

Before a satellite opens, the Administrator documents how it will share administration and supervision with the main office. This includes who answers phones, where the RN supervisor reports, and how the main-office Administrator will reach it.
The main-office Administrator (or Alternate) visits each satellite periodically, at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., monthly]. Each visit is logged with date, findings and follow-up.

Drop-off site: the Administrator verifies before use that the site will be used only as a staff work station. No prospective clients are met there, no billing is done there, no client records are kept there, and no sign or advertisement uses the agency name at that address.
Staff assigned to a drop-off site sign an acknowledgment of these limits. The Administrator audits the site at least quarterly and records the audit.
Change of address, counties served, or office opening or closing: the Administrator files Form 3110-1011 (or 3110-1011OL) with AHCA before making the change effective.

For an address change, the Administrator attaches evidence that the new location is properly zoned and proof of the agency's legal right to occupy it (lease, deed or equivalent). A copy is kept in the licensure file.
For any change in application or insurance information, the Administrator reports it to AHCA within 21 calendar days. The date sent and AHCA's confirmation are logged.

The Administrator updates the agency's license display, advertising, client notices, the hotline notice packet (CR-07), and the CEMP emergency contact information (SAF-04) to match the change. Updates are completed on or before the effective date.
Clients receiving services are told of any address, phone number or office change in writing, at least [NUMBER] days before it takes effect where possible.

Change of ownership: the current licensee and the new owner agree in writing on a closing date. The new owner files the required AHCA application before the transfer takes effect, and the agency does not operate under the new owner until AHCA approves.

On transfer, the Administrator transfers all client records, including active and closed files, to the new owner. A transfer log lists each record transferred, the date, and who received it. Records are moved securely under CR-03 and REC-04.
Clients, payers and referral sources are notified of the ownership change in writing, and clients are told they may choose another provider. Notices are kept in the licensure file.

Homemaker and companion registrants: the Administrator submits the renewal or change-of-ownership application at least 60 days before the registration expires. Any county served must be within the health service planning district of the address of record. See GOV-08.

If a filing deadline is missed, the Administrator reports the lapse to the governing body at once, files immediately, and records the corrective step. The agency understands that failure to apply for a change of ownership can result in administrative fines.
The Administrator keeps a copy of each filing, AHCA's response, and the proof of delivery in the licensure file for the life of the license plus the retention period in REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Approves or denies each change and confirms funding and insurance remain adequate.
Makes all AHCA filings on time, keeps evidence of zoning and right to occupy, and ensures satellites and drop-off sites comply.
Performs satellite visits and filings in the Administrator's absence.
Follow drop-off site limits, update notices and contact information, and assist with record transfers.

documentation: Change proposals and governing body minutes
Copies of Form 3110-1011 or 3110-1011OL filings, zoning evidence, proof of legal right to occupy, and AHCA correspondence
Satellite visit logs and drop-off site audits
Staff acknowledgments of drop-off site limits
Client record transfer logs for ownership change
Client, payer and referral source notices

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Services Provider Registration (Registrant Track)
policies.applies_to: Owners, Administrator, managing employee, office staff and caregivers of [AGENCY NAME] when operating under AHCA Homemaker and Companion Services registration rather than a Home Health Agency license.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is registered with AHCA before offering homemaker or companion services, keeps the registration current, verifies every worker's employment history, advertises correctly, and never provides hands-on personal care under a registration.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not provide homemaker or companion services to elderly or disabled adults until AHCA has registered it. It will keep registration current, verify the employment history of every worker with documented diligent effort, place the registration number in every advertisement, and refer clients who need hands-on help to a licensed Home Health Agency or nurse registry. A licensed Home Health Agency or nurse registry is exempt from separate registration for these services.

definitions.definition: Non-hands-on services such as companionship, conversation, meal preparation, light housekeeping, errands and reminders. They do not include bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, hygiene help, or transfers.
A provider registered with AHCA under s. 400.509, F.S. to provide homemaker and companion services.
Two documented attempts to verify a worker's employment or contractual history.
An AHCA notice listing missing items on an application. The applicant has 21 days to answer or the application is withdrawn.

procedures: Before offering services, the owner confirms that [AGENCY NAME] will provide only homemaker and companion services. If hands-on care is planned, a Home Health Agency license or nurse registry license is required instead, and the agency does not use this track.

The Administrator files AHCA Form 3110-1003 with the Addendum (Form 3110-1024) and the current fee. The fee is currently $50.75 for the biennium and $25 for a change, but the Administrator checks the form for the current amount before paying.

The application attests to Level 2 background screening of the owners, controlling interests, the Administrator or managing employee, and the financial officer. The Administrator confirms each person's screening is complete in the Clearinghouse before signing the attestation (see PER-02).
No homemaker or companion services are provided until AHCA issues the registration. The registration number and effective dates are recorded in the licensure file.
The Administrator calendars the expiration date. Registration is valid no more than 2 years. The renewal or change-of-ownership application is filed at least 60 days before expiration.
If AHCA sends an omission notice, the Administrator logs the date received, supplies the missing items, and responds in full within 21 days. The response and proof of delivery are filed.
Service area: the Administrator lists only counties within the health service planning district of the address of record. Any request outside that district is declined or referred (see GOV-07).

Before a worker has client contact, the Administrator or designee verifies the worker's employment history and records the source, date and result. If verification fails on the first attempt, a second attempt is made and documented. Two documented attempts constitute diligent effort.

Verification records are placed in the worker's personnel file under PER-07. A worker whose history cannot be verified after diligent effort is reviewed by the Administrator, and the decision and reason are recorded in the file.

The registration number is printed on every advertisement, flyer, website page, social media post and business card. Before publishing, the Administrator reviews each item and initials the review log (see GOV-02).

At intake the screener asks whether the client needs or is likely to need hands-on help (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, hygiene, transfers). Companion and homemaker clients receive only the services in the written service agreement (CR-06, SVC-01).

If a client needs hands-on help, the registrant does not provide it. The Administrator gives the client the names of licensed Home Health Agencies and nurse registries, documents the referral, and with the client's consent follows up.
Caregivers who see a client attempt a hands-on task, or a client asking for one, must decline and report to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator records the event.
The registrant accepts a client only if services can be provided adequately and safely, and the agency can supply capable staff for all scheduled visits. The intake decision is documented (SVC-02).
The agency keeps a confidential client record for each client containing the items the registration rule requires (REC-01, CR-03).
The Administrator reviews this policy and registration status annually and reports to the owner.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures registration is obtained and renewed on time and that the agency stays within the registrant scope.
Files AHCA forms, answers omission notices, verifies worker employment history, and reviews advertising.
Screen for hands-on needs and make referrals when needed.
Provide only homemaker and companion tasks and report requests for hands-on help.

documentation: Form 3110-1003, Addendum Form 3110-1024, fee receipt, registration certificate and AHCA correspondence
Omission notice log and responses
Level 2 screening confirmations for owners, managing employee and financial officer
Employment history verification records, including both attempts
Advertising review log
Referral records for clients needing hands-on help

policies.title: Discontinuance of Operation and Records Custody
policies.applies_to: Owners, governing body, Administrator, Alternate Administrator, RN Supervisor and records staff.
policies.purpose: To ensure that if [AGENCY NAME] closes, AHCA and clients are notified on time, clients are transitioned safely, the license is returned, and client records are kept safe and available for the full retention period.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will notify AHCA at least 30 days before discontinuing operation and will notify clients in advance. It will return the license on discontinuance. The licensee remains responsible for retaining and distributing client records for the required retention period, and will either forward each record as the client chooses or publish the required public notice. Client information is safeguarded throughout under HIPAA.

definitions.definition: The permanent end of the agency's operation, including closure, sale without transfer of license, or surrender of the license.
The continuing legal responsibility to keep client records secure, retrievable and confidential for the full retention period after closure.

procedures: The governing body decides on closure by written resolution that sets a target closure date at least 30 days out. The resolution is filed in the governance binder.

The Administrator sends written notice to AHCA at least 30 days before the closure date. The letter goes to the Laboratory and In-Home Services Unit, 2727 Mahan Drive, MS 32, Tallahassee, FL 32308, and the agency also contacts the unit at (850) 412-4500 to confirm receipt. A dated copy and proof of delivery are kept.
The Administrator prepares a list of all active clients, their services, payers, and the RN supervisor's current assessment of each client's needs.

The Administrator notifies each client (or guardian) in writing of the closure date and the plan for their care. Notice is delivered in the client's preferred language (CR-05) and also by phone to clients with high needs. Delivery is recorded.
Notice is also sent to referral sources, Medicaid plans, APD, the Area Agency on Aging and other payers, and to any caregiver or family contact on file.
Because the agency ceases operation, the Administrator also follows the emergency plan requirement to notify clients when the agency stops operating (SAF-04).
The RN Supervisor and Administrator help each client transition to another licensed provider of the client's choice, giving a care summary with the client's written consent.
Staff are told the closure date in writing, final pay is arranged in line with PER-08, and personnel records are secured under PER-07.

The Administrator decides how records will be distributed. With each client's choice, the record is forwarded to the client, the attending physician, or the client's current provider. A transfer log notes date, recipient and method.

For records not claimed or not forwarded, the Administrator publishes a notice at least once a week for 4 consecutive weeks in the newspaper of greatest circulation in the county. The notice states where and how records can be obtained. Tear sheets and proofs of publication are kept.

The Administrator designates a records custodian, [CUSTODIAN NAME AND ADDRESS], and a secure storage location that is access-controlled, protected from fire, water and unauthorized entry, and compliant with CR-03 and the HIPAA physical safeguards. The records remain retrievable and available for the required retention period set in REC-01.
If records are electronic, the Administrator arranges continued access, backup and security for the retention period, and records the vendor and location (REC-03).
On the final day of operation, the Administrator returns the license to AHCA and keeps proof of return.
The Administrator removes advertising, phone listings, web pages and signage, and posts a notice of where clients can obtain records.
The custodian responds to later record requests under REC-04 and keeps a log of all releases.
The Administrator completes a closure checklist, signs and dates it, and files it with the closure records.

responsibilities.duty: Decides on closure, funds record storage for the retention period, and remains responsible for custody.
Sends AHCA and client notices, returns the license, arranges transitions and distributes records.
Prepares clinical transition summaries and helps clients find new providers.
Secures records, logs requests and releases, and honors confidentiality.

documentation: Board resolution to close
AHCA notice letter and proof of delivery
Client, payer and referral source notices with delivery proof
Record transfer and release logs
Newspaper notice and proofs of publication
Custodian designation and storage description
License return proof and closure checklist

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All staff, caregivers and RN supervisors, and all clients and their representatives, under both the Home Health Agency license and the Homemaker and Companion registration.
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) (HCBS setting requirements, Medicaid waiver clients)
policies.purpose: To ensure that every client knows and can exercise his or her rights, and that staff protect those rights in daily care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] recognizes and protects the rights of every client. Each client is told of and may take part in care planning, may receive a copy of the plan on request, and is told in writing of these rights and the complaint, abuse and Medicaid fraud hotlines on or before the first day of service, with a signed acknowledgment. No client is retaliated against for exercising a right.

definitions.definition: A person receiving services from [AGENCY NAME], including his or her guardian or authorized representative where applicable.
The written description of the services the client will receive, developed with the client (see SVC-03).
For Medicaid HCBS clients, planning that reflects the client's choices, goals and preferences.

procedures: Before or at the first visit, and on or before the first day of service, the intake staff member gives each client or representative the written Client Rights and Responsibilities notice and the three hotline notices (complaint, abuse, Medicaid fraud). See CR-07 for the notice contents.
Staff review the rights notice aloud in plain language and in the client's preferred language, using interpreter or translation help as needed (CR-05). Staff confirm the client understands.

The client or representative signs and dates an acknowledgment. If the client cannot or will not sign, staff record the reason and a second staff member witnesses. The acknowledgment is placed in the client record.

The notice states that the client has the right to: be free from abuse, neglect and exploitation; be treated with dignity and respect; privacy and confidentiality; refuse any service; consent to or decline RN supervisory visits; consent in writing before any medication assistance; and report abuse, complaints and Medicaid fraud without retaliation.

The notice states that the client may be informed of the plan of care, take part in developing it, and receive a copy on request. The RN Supervisor or designee explains this at the assessment and each plan update (SVC-03).
The written service agreement (CR-06) states the services, rates for privately paid services, and payment sources. The client receives a copy before services start.

RN supervisory visits to the home are arranged based on the client's direction, approval and agreement to pay for them where payment is private. The RN explains the purpose of these visits, and the client's decision is recorded (SVC-04).

The client's right to refuse care is respected. When a client declines a task, the caregiver does not argue or pressure, informs the RN Supervisor the same day, and documents the refusal in the service note. The RN reviews whether the plan needs updating.
For medication assistance, no help is given until the client or representative has consented in writing (SVC-06).

Medicaid HCBS clients are also told of their plan or waiver rights, including choice of provider and person-centered planning. The Administrator confirms the agency's practices meet the payer's HCBS setting rules.
The client's rights regarding advance directives and do-not-resuscitate orders are explained under CR-08.
Clients are told how to file a complaint with the agency (CR-02) and with AHCA, and that no one will be retaliated against for doing so.

Client responsibilities are explained at the same time: giving accurate information, telling the agency of changes in health or schedule, providing a safe home environment, treating staff respectfully, and paying agreed charges.
Staff who learn of a possible rights violation report to the Administrator the same day. Abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under SAF-01.
The Administrator reviews rights complaints and incidents quarterly in QA meetings (GOV-04).
All new staff are trained on client rights during orientation, and annually thereafter (PER-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures notices are current, delivered on time and acknowledged, and reviews rights complaints.
Deliver and explain rights notices and hotline notices and obtain signatures.
Explains plan participation and supervisory visit options and respects client decisions.
Honor client rights daily, record refusals, and report violations.

documentation: Signed Client Rights and Responsibilities acknowledgment
Hotline notice delivery record with date
Signed service agreement
Documentation of client decisions on RN visits and medication help
Refusal-of-service entries in service notes
Training records on client rights

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All clients and their representatives, and all staff who receive or handle complaints.
federal: 42 CFR 438.402 (SMMC plan grievance system, for plan-enrolled clients)
policies.purpose: To give every client an easy, safe way to raise concerns, to make sure each is answered promptly and fairly, and to make sure clients know how to report complaints to AHCA.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] welcomes complaints and treats each as a chance to improve. On or before the first day of service, every client receives the statewide AHCA complaint number in legible form with the words 'To report a complaint regarding the services you receive, please call toll-free [AHCA COMPLAINT HOTLINE NUMBER – confirm the current number on AHCA's website before printing].' The agency keeps an internal grievance log, responds to each grievance, and does not retaliate against anyone who complains.

definitions.definition: Any complaint or expression of dissatisfaction by a client or representative about services, staff, billing or rights, made orally or in writing.
The agency record of each grievance, with date received, who received it, the response, and the resolution.
Any adverse action, such as reduced service, changed schedule, or hostile treatment, taken because of a complaint.

procedures: On or before the first day of service, intake staff give each client the complaint notice with the AHCA toll-free number, using the wording above. The Administrator verifies the current number on AHCA's website before each printing of the notice, and records the date verified.

Intake staff explain that the client may complain to the agency, to AHCA, to the Medicaid plan or payer, and to the abuse and Medicaid fraud hotlines (CR-07) at any time, with or without first telling the agency.
For Medicaid SMMC members, staff also give the plan's grievance and appeal contact information and the choice counseling number, 1-877-711-3662.
Any employee who receives a complaint, by phone, in person, in writing, or through a family member, writes it down the same day and gives it to the Administrator or Alternate within one business day.
The Administrator enters it in the grievance log with a number, date, client name, complainant, nature, staff involved, and priority.
Within 2 business days the Administrator acknowledges the complaint to the client in the client's preferred language, in person or by phone, and follows up in writing if the client requests.
Complaints involving abuse, neglect, exploitation or injury are immediately referred to SAF-01 and SAF-02 and reported as required. They are not held for the normal grievance process.

The Administrator investigates promptly, speaking with the client, the staff involved, and the RN Supervisor, and reviewing records. The investigation is completed within [NUMBER, e.g., 10] business days where possible.

The Administrator gives the client a written or verbal response stating what was found, what was done, and the client's right to take the matter to AHCA or the payer if not satisfied. The response is recorded in the log.
If a staff member is at fault, corrective action under PER-09 is taken and recorded in the personnel file.

Staff are told that retaliation against a complainant is not permitted. Any care changes after a complaint, such as a caregiver change, are made only with the client's agreement or for safety, and are reviewed by the Administrator.
The Administrator keeps the grievance log confidential, sharing client information only as allowed by CR-03.
If AHCA contacts the agency about a complaint, the Administrator cooperates, makes records available as required under GOV-06, and records the inquiry and outcome.
The Administrator summarizes grievances, trends and corrective actions quarterly to the QA committee (GOV-04) and the governing body.
Clients with disabilities or limited English receive help filing a grievance, including a staff member to write it down or an interpreter (CR-05).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the grievance process, logs, investigates and responds, and reports trends.
Receive and pass on all complaints within one business day and never retaliate.
Deliver the AHCA complaint number and payer contacts on or before the first day of service.
Reviews grievance summaries and ensures corrective action.

documentation: Complaint notice with AHCA number and record of delivery date
Record of verification of the current AHCA complaint number
Grievance log with response and resolution
Investigation notes and corrective action records
Quarterly grievance summaries to the QA committee

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers and students of [AGENCY NAME], and all client records in any form.
policies.purpose: To protect the confidentiality of client information as Florida and federal law require, and to define when and how information may be shared.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not disclose information from a client's file without the written consent of the client or guardian, except as the law allows. All information about a client that employees, contractors, or AHCA receive is confidential and exempt from Florida's public records law (ch. 119, F.S.). Registrants keep a confidential client record. A client who transfers to another home health agency receives a copy of the record on request. The agency complies with the HIPAA Privacy and Security rules and stores client data only in the locations permitted by its license application.

definitions.definition: Individually identifiable health or care information about a client, in any form.
A signed and dated authorization from the client or guardian that states what may be released, to whom, and for how long.
The notice that tells clients how the agency may use and disclose PHI and their rights.

procedures: The Administrator is designated Privacy Officer unless the governing body names another person: [PRIVACY OFFICER NAME]. The designation is in writing.
At or before the first visit, staff give each client the Notice of Privacy Practices and obtain a signed acknowledgment, which is placed in the client record.

All new employees, contractors and volunteers sign a confidentiality agreement before access to any client information and are trained in privacy and security during orientation (PER-03). Training is repeated annually.
Staff access client information only as needed for their job. They do not discuss clients in public places, on social media, or with anyone not involved in the care.

Before any disclosure outside the agency, staff obtain a written, signed and dated consent from the client or guardian, except where law allows disclosure without it (for example, mandatory abuse reporting under SAF-01 and AHCA survey access under REC-04). The consent is filed in the record.

Requests for information from family, physicians, payers, lawyers or other agencies are directed to the Administrator, who verifies identity and authority, checks for valid consent, and records the release (REC-04).
When a client transfers to another home health agency and requests it, the Administrator sends a copy of the record promptly. The transfer is logged with date, recipient and contents (REC-04).
Registrant track: the agency keeps a confidential client record for each client with the contents required by the registration rule (REC-01).
Paper records are kept in locked cabinets in the office. Records are not left in vehicles or homes. Caregivers carrying client information keep it with them or secured and return it to the office.
Electronic records use unique user IDs, passwords, automatic log-off and role-based access. The Administrator removes access on the day a person leaves (REC-03).

Client data may be stored offsite or in the cloud only within the continental United States, its territories, or Canada, consistent with the attestation made in the agency's license application. Before using any new vendor or system, the Administrator confirms the data location in writing and records it (REC-03).
Text messages, email and phone calls about clients use only agency-approved methods, with the minimum information needed. Personal phones are used only as allowed by the Administrator.
Staff report any suspected privacy breach, such as a lost record, misdirected message or unauthorized access, to the Privacy Officer within 24 hours.

The Privacy Officer investigates, limits harm, documents the findings, and determines whether notice to the client or others is required under federal rules. Corrective action, including discipline under PER-09, is taken.
The Privacy Officer reviews privacy practices yearly and reports to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees privacy and security, approves disclosures, investigates breaches and trains staff.
Keep client information confidential, obtain consent before disclosure, and report breaches within 24 hours.
Deliver the Notice of Privacy Practices and obtain acknowledgment.
Approves privacy policies and receives annual and breach reports.

documentation: Privacy Officer designation
Signed Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgments
Staff confidentiality agreements and training records
Signed client consents to release information
Record release and transfer logs
Data location confirmation for electronic systems and vendors
Breach reports, investigations and corrective actions

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
policies.applies_to: All employees, contracted staff, home health aides/CNAs, homemakers, companions, RN supervisors, administrator and alternate administrator
policies.purpose: To protect each client's property and finances, to prevent financial exploitation by staff, and to make sure any suspected exploitation is reported immediately.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] respects each client's privacy and property. Employees may not hold or manage client funds, accept gifts beyond a nominal token, borrow from or lend to clients, or be named in client legal or financial documents. They may not accept bequests or powers of attorney from clients. A client's card or cash may be used only for an itemized errand the client has authorized, and every errand must be backed by a receipt. Any suspected financial exploitation is reported at once to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, and the administrator is notified. Aide training includes respect for the client's privacy and property (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)8, F.A.C.).

definitions.definition: Improper use of a client's funds, property or assets, or obtaining them through deception, undue influence or coercion, for the benefit of someone other than the client.
A small, non-cash token such as a card, a homemade treat or a flower, worth $10 or less, that is given freely and not in exchange for favors or better service.
A shopping or similar task the client has authorized in the service agreement or plan, handled with receipts and a reconciliation of the money used.

procedures: At orientation and again at annual in-service, the administrator or RN supervisor trains each employee on this policy, including respect for client privacy and property, and records the training in the personnel file (PER-03).

Each employee signs an acknowledgment that they will not hold client funds, accept gifts above the limit, borrow or lend, or be named in client documents. The acknowledgment is placed in the personnel file (PER-07).

During intake, the intake coordinator tells each client and representative about this policy and the client's right to have property treated with respect (CR-01), and gives them the contact information to report a concern (CR-02, CR-07).
Before any errand, the client or representative states what is to be bought and approves a spending limit. The employee records this on the Errand and Receipt Log.
The employee uses the client's cash or card only for the approved errand. The employee never keeps the card, PIN, checkbook or account passwords and never uses a client's card for personal purchases.
The employee gets an itemized receipt, returns the card and all change to the client, and has the client sign the Errand and Receipt Log the same day. The employee attaches the receipt to the log.
The RN supervisor reviews errand logs and receipts at each supervisory visit and at least monthly for any client with regular errands. The review is documented in the client record.

Employees decline gifts of money, jewelry, valuables, vehicles or property in any amount. They may accept a nominal gift only if declining would hurt the client, and must report it to the administrator within 24 hours for entry in the Gift Log.
Employees may not borrow money or items from a client, lend money to a client, sell items to or buy items from a client, or ask a client for loans, donations or investments.

Employees may not witness, draft or be named in a client's will, trust, power of attorney, joint account, beneficiary designation or other legal or financial document. [AGENCY NAME] does not accept bequests or powers of attorney from clients. An employee who is asked must decline and report the request to the administrator the same day.

Employees do not move, give away or dispose of client belongings except as the client directs and the plan of care documents. They report lost, missing or damaged property to the RN supervisor the same day.

The administrator opens a property concern file for each report of missing or damaged property. The administrator interviews the client, representative and employee, and completes an incident report (SAF-02) within 24 hours.

Any employee who suspects financial exploitation reports it immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 and notifies the administrator right after. The administrator follows SAF-01 and may not delay, screen or discourage the report.

The administrator removes any employee under investigation for exploitation from that client's case until the matter is resolved. The administrator cooperates with DCF, law enforcement and AHCA and documents all actions.

The administrator reviews the Gift Log, Errand and Receipt Logs and property concern files at least quarterly and reports trends to the QA committee (GOV-04). Substantiated violations lead to discipline up to termination (PER-09).

responsibilities.duty: Enforces this policy, investigates property concerns, ensures reports are made, keeps the Gift Log, and reports trends to QA.
Reviews errand logs and receipts, reinforces expectations during supervisory visits, and reports concerns to the administrator.
Follows the limits on gifts, funds and documents; completes errand logs; reports exploitation concerns immediately.
Informs clients and representatives of this policy at intake.

documentation: Employee signed acknowledgment (personnel file)
Training records (orientation and annual in-service)
Errand and Receipt Log with receipts and client signatures
Gift Log
Property concern file and incident report
Abuse Hotline report confirmation, if made
Quarterly QA review summary

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
policies.applies_to: All employees, contracted staff, intake coordinator, RN supervisors, scheduler, administrator and alternate administrator
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act, 42 U.S.C. 2000d
ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. 12181 et seq.
policies.purpose: To make sure every person has equal access to [AGENCY NAME]'s services, and that clients can communicate effectively with staff.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (including limited English proficiency), disability, age, sex, religion or any other protected status. Acceptance of a client depends on whether services can reasonably be provided safely in the home, including whether we can communicate with the client through a same-language staff person, an interpreter, or translation technology (Rule 59A-8.020(1), F.A.C.). This is a duty to provide communication access. It is not a reason to refuse a client because of the language they speak. The agency provides language assistance and auxiliary aids to clients and representatives at no cost.

definitions.definition: A person who does not speak English as a primary language and has a limited ability to read, speak, write or understand English.
A person who is fluent in English and the client's language, is trained in interpreting, and is impartial. A client's minor child is not used as an interpreter.
Services that make communication effective for people with disabilities, such as sign language interpreters, large print, captioning and screen-reader compatible materials.
Short notices in other languages telling people that language assistance is free and how to get it.

procedures: The administrator designates a language access coordinator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME] unless another person is named in writing) who maintains the list of bilingual staff, interpreter vendors and translation tools.
