If no response is received, the coordinator makes a second attempt on a different day, by a different method if possible. If a number is disconnected, the coordinator tries to find current contact information and records that effort.

Each attempt is recorded on the Employment History Verification Form with the date, time, method, person or entity contacted, result and the coordinator's initials. Two documented attempts meet diligent effort when no response comes.
The Administrator reviews any gaps, negative references or inconsistencies before the person is scheduled and records the decision in the file.
The coordinator enters each employee's 5-year rescreening due date in the screening tracking log and reviews the log monthly.
Rescreening is started at least 90 days before the due date. An employee whose rescreening is not complete by the due date is removed from client contact until it is complete.
Employees must report any arrest or charge to the Administrator within one business day. The Administrator reviews it with the Clearinghouse record and decides on continued assignment.
Questions about Clearinghouse status are directed to the AHCA Background Screening Unit at 850-412-4503 or bgscreen@ahca.myflorida.com.
The Administrator audits screening and verification records quarterly and reports results to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures owners and administrators are screened and that screening is funded.
Ensures no one has client contact before clearance, decides on any adverse findings and notifies AHCA of administrator changes.
Submits screening, tracks rescreening, and completes and documents employment verification.
Complete screening honestly and report arrests or charges promptly.

documentation: Clearinghouse eligibility results and fingerprint receipts
Employment History Verification Form with two documented attempts
Screening and rescreening tracking log
Owner, administrator and financial officer screening records
Notice to AHCA of administrator changes
Administrator decisions on any adverse findings

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
policies.applies_to: All home health aides, CNAs and other direct-care staff; Homemaker and Companion registrant staff for the items that apply to their duties
policies.purpose: To make sure all caregivers are trained and competent before assignment and stay current through annual in-service training, CPR and required one-time courses.
policies.policy: Before assignment, each aide must have completed 40 hours of training covering the required subject areas, or have passed the competency test (see PER-04). Anyone who will assist with medication must also complete 2 hours of medication assistance training that includes a label-reading check (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c), F.A.C.). Each calendar year, every aide must complete in-service training, and must hold current CPR certification with an in-person skills demonstration (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(k)). Dementia training under s. 430.5025, F.S., and the HIV/AIDS course are completed as described in PER-05. [AGENCY NAME] also gives annual bloodborne pathogen training to employees with occupational exposure under federal OSHA rules. All training is documented in the personnel file.

definitions.definition: Agency-specific training on policies, client rights, reporting duties, safety and the employee's role, completed before the first client assignment.
Continuing education given each calendar year to keep aides current.
Observed demonstration of aide skills by an RN (or LPN under RN supervision).

An instructor or provider approved by the American Red Cross, American Heart Association, National Safety Council, or an organization accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Pre-Hospital Continuing Education.

procedures: After PER-01 and PER-02 are complete, the RN Supervisor schedules the new employee's orientation. No client assignment may occur before orientation is done.

Orientation covers at least: the agency's policies and this manual, client rights (CR-01), abuse/neglect reporting (SAF-01), incident reporting (SAF-02), infection control (SAF-03), emergency procedures (SVC-10, SAF-04), privacy (CR-03), scope of duties (SVC-01), EVV and timekeeping (SVC-09) and professional boundaries (PER-09).

The RN Supervisor confirms that the employee has either 40 hours of documented training in the required subject areas or a passed competency test. If not, the employee follows PER-04 before assignment.

If the employee will assist with medication, the RN Supervisor confirms the 2-hour medication assistance course, including the label-reading check, is complete and signed. Without it, the employee may not assist with medication (SVC-06).

The RN Supervisor or designee observes the new aide in person demonstrating the skills the client plan will require (e.g., bathing, transfers, feeding, toileting, vital signs if applicable). The evaluator signs and dates the Competency Observation Checklist.
Competency on any task the aide has not previously been observed doing is validated before the aide performs it independently. Gaps are corrected with added training and re-observation.

Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other infectious materials receive bloodborne pathogen training at hire and annually, as required by 29 CFR 1910.1030. Sign-in sheets and content are kept.

The coordinator tracks each employee's annual in-service status by calendar year. The agency plans in-service sessions covering topics such as infection control, client rights, abuse reporting, safe transfers, dementia care, emergency preparedness and documentation.

Every aide completes the annual in-service each calendar year. Hours and topics are recorded on the In-Service Record with the date, instructor and signature. The Administrator sets a deadline of November 30 to leave time to make up missed sessions.

Every aide holds current CPR certification from an approved provider, with an in-person skills demonstration. Online-only CPR does not satisfy this policy. The coordinator files a copy of the card and tracks its expiration.
An aide whose CPR certification lapses is not scheduled for client care until it is renewed, unless the Administrator documents an approved short extension in line with the rule.
Dementia and HIV/AIDS training is tracked as set out in PER-05.
The RN Supervisor reviews any performance concern, complaint or incident for retraining needs and documents additional training provided.
The Administrator reviews training compliance quarterly and reports results to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Provides resources, ensures compliance with training requirements and reviews training reports.
Conducts or oversees orientation, evaluates competency and plans in-service.
Tracks due dates for in-service and CPR and keeps training records.
Attends all training, maintains CPR and asks for retraining when unsure.

documentation: Orientation checklist signed by employee and trainer
Competency Observation Checklist
Medication assistance course record (2 hours, with label-reading check)
In-Service Records with date, topic, hours, instructor
CPR card copies and tracking log
Bloodborne pathogen training records

policies.title: Home Health Aide Training Course and Competency Test Program
policies.applies_to: Home Health Agency (non-skilled) preparing aides through agency training or competency testing
policies.purpose: To set the rules for how [AGENCY NAME] trains or tests home health aides so that every aide is qualified under Rule 59A-8.0095 before assignment, and the agency does not misrepresent its training or charge improper fees.
policies.policy: Aide training given by the agency is delivered by or under the general supervision of a registered nurse with at least 2 years of nursing experience, at least one of them in home health care. Training may be in person, online or hybrid, but the aide must demonstrate skills in person. As an alternative to the 40-hour course, an aide may pass the competency test (AHCA Form 3110-1007, Sept 2025): all 14 practical tasks observed and evaluated by an RN, or an LPN under RN supervision, and at least 90 of 104 written questions correct. [AGENCY NAME] is not an approved nonpublic postsecondary career school unless stated otherwise by the Governing Body, and therefore follows the limits in Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(g) and (h).

definitions.definition: AHCA Form 3110-1007, with a practical part of 14 tasks and a written part of 104 questions.
The title required on training records issued by an agency that teaches the course.
The RN is responsible for the course content and trainers and is available to the trainer, though not always present.

procedures: The Administrator designates an RN Supervisor who meets the experience requirement (RN with at least 2 years of nursing experience, one in home health) to direct all aide training and testing. The RN's license and experience are verified and filed.

Each trainee is enrolled on a Training Roster showing name, start date, delivery method and trainer. Trainees are told in writing that they are applicants or employees of the agency and that the agency does not charge a fee for the course.

Training covers the subject areas required by Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c). Instruction is by the RN or by persons under the RN's general supervision, using a written curriculum approved by the RN Supervisor.
If part of the course is online or hybrid, the trainee must still demonstrate skills in person. The RN or a qualified designee observes and signs off on each skill.
The agency keeps training records titled 'Home Health Aide Documentation'. Each record includes the agency name, license number, student information, hours per topic and the trainer's signature.

The agency does not issue any document called a diploma, certificate, certification of completion or transcript, does not charge tuition or fees for the course, and does not advertise 'training for home health aides.' Recruiting ads may say only that the agency is hiring aides and intends to provide training (GOV-02).

For the competency test, the RN Supervisor schedules the practical part. An RN, or an LPN under the RN's supervision, observes and scores all 14 practical tasks on Form 3110-1007. The evaluator signs and dates the form.
The written part of 104 questions may be given by any staff member in a quiet setting without assistance. The staff member who gave the test signs the form. The score is recorded.
To pass, the aide must complete all 14 practical tasks successfully and answer at least 90 of the 104 written questions correctly. The RN Supervisor reviews the result and records pass or fail.

If the aide fails, the RN Supervisor decides, at the agency's discretion, whether and when a retake is allowed, and whether added training is needed first. The decision and any added training are documented.
An aide who passes the competency test is not allowed to assist with medication unless the 2-hour medication assistance course (with label-reading check) is also complete (PER-03, SVC-06).

For an aide trained elsewhere, the RN Supervisor reviews the paperwork and validates the aide's competency in person by observing skills before first assignment. The validation is documented and signed.

The RN Supervisor reviews training content annually and updates it when rules or agency practices change. The Administrator keeps the current version of Form 3110-1007 and replaces superseded versions.
Completed rosters, test forms and training records are filed in the personnel file (PER-07) and are available for surveyor review.

responsibilities.duty: Designates a qualified RN to lead training, ensures no fees are charged and no prohibited wording is used in documents or ads.
Directs training, observes and scores practical skills, validates outside training and signs records.
Administers the written part fairly and records the score.
Attends training, demonstrates skills in person and completes the test honestly.

documentation: RN Supervisor credential and experience verification
Training Roster and curriculum
'Home Health Aide Documentation' record with agency name, license number, student information, hours per topic and trainer signature
Completed Form 3110-1007 (practical and written) with scores and signatures
Retake and added-training records
Validation record for aides trained elsewhere

policies.title: Dementia-Related Training and HIV/AIDS Education
policies.applies_to: All home health agency, nurse registry and homemaker/companion staff with client contact
policies.purpose: To make sure caregivers receive the dementia-related and HIV/AIDS training Florida requires, on time and with proof on file.
policies.policy: All staff with client contact receive basic dementia information at hire. Within 30 days of hire, they complete a 1-hour dementia course, and within 7 months of hire they complete 2 additional hours, as required by s. 430.5025, F.S., and s. 400.4785, F.S. Every home health agency employee completes a one-time HIV/AIDS education course within 30 days of employment (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(r), F.A.C.). If [AGENCY NAME] claims to provide special care for persons with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, it discloses the services that make it suitable for those clients, as required by s. 400.4785(2), F.S. (see SVC-13).

definitions.definition: Training on Alzheimer's disease and related disorders under s. 430.5025, F.S., consisting of a 1-hour course and 2 additional hours.
A short introduction given at hire that covers recognizing dementia, communication and safety.
A one-time education course completed by each employee within 30 days of employment.

procedures: On the first day of orientation, the trainer gives each new employee the basic dementia information and records the date on the training log.

The Training Coordinator enters the employee's hire date and calculates three due dates in the tracking log: 30 days (1-hour dementia course), 30 days (HIV/AIDS course) and 7 months (2 additional dementia hours).
The coordinator assigns the 1-hour dementia course within the first week of employment, using an approved course. Free online options through the Department of Elder Affairs may be used.
The employee completes the 1-hour course within 30 days of hire and gives the coordinator the completion certificate or record on the same day.

The coordinator assigns the HIV/AIDS course within the first week of employment. The employee completes it within 30 days of hire and files the certificate. A comparable course taken within a prior period may be accepted only if the Administrator confirms it meets the rule and documents that decision.
The coordinator assigns the 2 additional hours of dementia training. The employee completes them within 7 months of hire and files the record.
The coordinator checks the tracking log weekly. Employees who are within 10 days of a deadline receive a written reminder and a copy to their supervisor.

An employee who misses the 30-day deadline is told in writing that it is overdue. The Administrator decides whether client assignments are limited until completion, and records the decision. Employees are not assigned to clients with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders until the 1-hour course is complete, unless the RN Supervisor documents a safe arrangement.
Dementia training is also reflected in client care. The RN Supervisor ensures plans of care for clients with dementia address communication, wandering, behavior and safety (SVC-13).

If the agency advertises or states that it offers special Alzheimer's care, the Administrator prepares a written disclosure of the services and staff training that make it suitable, gives it to prospective clients, and keeps it on file. If the agency does not provide special care, it does not make that claim (GOV-02).
All certificates and completion records are copied into the personnel file (PER-07) and kept in line with the agency's retention schedule (REC-01).
The Administrator reviews the tracking log monthly. Compliance rates and late completions are reported to the QA committee (GOV-04).

Staff who work only as companions or homemakers follow the same dementia training timeline, and the HIV/AIDS course is assigned to them as a best practice, even though the rule specifically applies to home health agency employees.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures training is available, approves any limits on assignments for overdue training and approves the Alzheimer's care disclosure.
Calculates due dates, assigns courses, reminds employees and files certificates.
Reflects dementia training in care plans and observes the use of dementia care techniques.
Completes each course by its deadline and submits proof.

documentation: Training tracking log with hire date and three due dates
Certificates or course records for 1-hour dementia course, 2 additional hours and HIV/AIDS course
Written reminders and overdue notices
Alzheimer's care disclosure, if the agency claims special care
Administrator decisions on overdue training

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All direct-care staff (home health aides, CNAs, homemakers, companions), RN supervisors, administrator and alternate administrator; Home Health Agency (non-skilled) and Homemaker and Companion registrant
federal: CDC healthcare personnel TB guidance (used as a reference; not regulatory for non-skilled home health agencies)
policies.purpose: To protect clients and staff from communicable disease by setting an agency-adopted, risk-based employee health program, including TB screening, hepatitis B vaccination where blood exposure is anticipated, and return-to-work rules for illness and exposure.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates an internal employee health program for all direct-care staff. Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C., sets the personnel requirements for aides. As of the date this policy was adopted, the agency has not identified a Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. rule that requires TB testing or physical examinations for aides of a non-skilled agency. The requirements below are therefore agency-adopted standards based on risk, and they are not a claim that the rule requires them. Payers, Medicaid plans, Area Agencies on Aging, assisted living facilities and other contracts may require more, including specific TB tests, physicals or vaccinations. When a contract requires more, the stricter requirement applies. The agency will not allow staff with signs or symptoms of a communicable disease to work with clients. Employee health information is confidential and is kept separate from the personnel file. The agency applies this policy consistently and will provide reasonable accommodation as required by law.

definitions.definition: Any employee who provides hands-on personal care, homemaker services or companion services in a client's home.
A symptom questionnaire plus, at baseline, a TB test (interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) or tuberculin skin test (TST)) interpreted by a licensed health care provider.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials during assigned duties, for example assisting with a client who has bleeding, a wound or a colostomy bag.
An illness that can spread from person to person, such as influenza, COVID-19, norovirus, scabies, or suspected or confirmed active TB.

procedures: The Administrator designates the RN Supervisor as the employee health coordinator and records the designation in the policy file.

After a conditional offer of employment and before the employee's first client contact, the employee completes the Employee Health Questionnaire. It asks about TB symptoms, communicable illness and ability to perform the essential duties with or without reasonable accommodation. The RN Supervisor reviews it within 2 business days.

Each year the RN Supervisor performs and documents a written TB risk assessment. It considers the client population served, community TB incidence information from the county health department, and any contractual requirements.

As a baseline for new direct-care staff, the agency requires a TB test (IGRA or TST) performed by a licensed provider, or documentation of a prior positive result with a negative symptom screen. The result must be on file before the first client visit. The employee may submit results from a prior employer if they are dated within 12 months before hire.

If a test is positive, the employee must have a provider evaluation, which normally includes a chest X-ray. The employee may not work with clients until a licensed provider states in writing that the employee is not infectious. Employees with a documented positive test are not retested; they complete a symptom screen annually.
Each year the RN Supervisor collects a TB symptom screen from every direct-care employee, and repeats TB testing only after a known exposure or when a contract requires it.

Before accepting any new payer, plan, AAA or facility contract, the Administrator reviews it for employee health requirements (TB tests, physicals, vaccinations, immunizations). The Administrator records the requirements in the contract file and applies the stricter standard to affected staff.

Where occupational exposure to blood is anticipated, the agency offers the hepatitis B vaccination series at no cost to the employee within 10 working days of initial assignment. An employee who declines signs the declination statement. An employee who declines may request the vaccine later at no cost.

The agency maintains a written exposure control plan. It covers gloves and other personal protective equipment, hand hygiene, safe handling of sharps and contaminated items, and post-exposure evaluation and follow-up at no cost to the employee. The plan is reviewed annually and the training is repeated at annual in-service (PER-03; SAF-03).

An employee must report to the supervisor before the start of the shift if the employee has fever, persistent cough, vomiting, diarrhea, a new rash or draining skin lesion, or any known exposure to a communicable disease. The employee must not enter a client's home until the supervisor has evaluated the report.

Unless a health care provider or the county health department directs otherwise, the supervisor applies these exclusion standards. For fever, the employee stays out until fever-free for 24 hours without fever-reducing medication. For vomiting or diarrhea, the employee stays out until symptom-free for 48 hours. For infestations such as scabies or lice, the employee stays out until treated. For suspected TB, the employee stays out until cleared in writing by a licensed provider.

When an employee is excluded, the supervisor reassigns or covers the visits and notifies affected clients under the missed-visit procedures in SVC-08. The supervisor also tells the client what to do if the client has been exposed to a staff member with a contagious illness.

If a staff member or client is exposed to a reportable communicable disease, the RN Supervisor consults the county health department, follows its direction, and documents the exposure, the notifications made and the follow-up.

An employee may return to work when symptoms have resolved under the standards above, or on a written release from a licensed provider when the supervisor requests one. The supervisor documents the return date. No employee will be disciplined or retaliated against for reporting an illness or exposure in good faith.

Employee medical information (TB results, vaccination or declination forms, provider releases, exposure reports) is kept in a locked medical file or restricted electronic folder separate from the personnel file. Only the Administrator and RN Supervisor may access it, except as required by law. Records related to occupational exposure are kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years, as required by the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard.
The RN Supervisor reviews this program each year with the QAPI committee (GOV-04) and updates it for changes in contracts, CDC guidance or exposure incidents.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the program, ensures baseline requirements are met before first visits, reviews payer contracts for health requirements, and protects confidentiality of medical files.
Reviews questionnaires and test results, performs the annual risk assessment, directs exclusion and return-to-work decisions, and coordinates exposure follow-up with the county health department.
Does not schedule an employee for client visits until the Administrator confirms baseline health requirements are on file, and covers visits when an employee is excluded.
Complete required screening, report illness and exposure before shifts, follow exclusion rules, and use personal protective equipment.

documentation: Employee Health Questionnaire (in the confidential medical file)
Baseline TB test result or prior positive documentation and annual symptom screens
Annual TB risk assessment
Hepatitis B vaccine record or signed declination
Exposure incident reports and post-exposure follow-up
Illness reports, exclusion and return-to-work records
Contract health-requirement checklist

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All employees and any contracted staff; Home Health Agency (non-skilled) and Homemaker and Companion registrant
policies.purpose: To ensure each employee has a complete, accurate and retrievable personnel file, and that an aide's file is complete before the aide serves any client, so the agency can demonstrate compliance to surveyors at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel file for every employee and every person who provides services to clients. Before an aide's first client visit, the file must show the qualifications Florida requires: either 40 hours of aide training or a passed competency test; current Florida CNA certification or a copy of another state's current certificate (where the aide is a CNA); medication assistance training; current CPR certification; Level 2 background screening results and employment history verification. Files also contain the annual in-service record, HIV/AIDS education and dementia-related training, as applicable. The file of an administrator or alternate administrator also contains the written designation. Personnel files are available for review by surveyors during unannounced surveys. The agency does not schedule any employee for client visits until the Administrator signs the file completion checklist.

definitions.definition: The complete record of an individual's qualifications, screening, training, employment and performance. Medical and I-9 documents are kept in separate confidential files.
A signed form showing each required item is present, current and dated before the employee's first client visit.
Fingerprint-based background screening required under s. 408.809, F.S., repeated every 5 years.

procedures: At hire, the Administrator or designee opens a personnel file using the standard file index and a File Completion Checklist for the employee's position.

The Administrator or designee verifies and files the aide qualification. For home health aides, the file contains either (a) the training record showing 40 hours of aide training, or (b) the competency test result showing all 14 practical tasks and at least 90 of 104 written questions passed on the AHCA competency test form. Where training or testing was delivered online or hybrid, the file also contains documentation that skills were demonstrated in person.

For a certified nursing assistant, the file contains a copy of the current Florida CNA certification, or a copy of the current certificate from another state. The designee checks the certification status with the issuing registry, prints or screenshots the result with the date, and sets a tickler for the expiration date.
The file contains a record of the 2 hours of medication-assistance training, which includes a label-reading check, before the aide assists any client with medications (SVC-06).
The file contains a copy of a current CPR certification. The designee sets a tickler to obtain the renewal before expiration.

The file contains the Level 2 screening result for the employee, dated, and a tickler for the 5-year rescreen. The agency does not allow a person to provide direct care until the result shows eligibility (PER-02).

The file contains the employment history verification and notes of each attempt made to verify prior employment. Where a prior employer does not respond, the designee documents at least two dated attempts (PER-02).
The file contains the HIV/AIDS education record. It must be completed within 30 days of hire. The designee sets a 30-day tickler (PER-05).
The file contains dementia-related training records where the employee serves or may serve clients with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders (PER-05; SVC-13).

The designee adds the annual in-service record each calendar year, showing date, topic, hours and instructor, and keeps the record current. An aide who has not completed the calendar-year in-service is not scheduled after the due date until it is completed (PER-03).
For the Administrator and alternate administrator, the file contains the written designation, and the alternate's written on-site designation, signed and dated by the governing body (GOV-01).

The Administrator completes the employee's Form I-9 verification. The employee completes Section 1 no later than the first day of work, and the agency completes Section 2 within 3 business days of the start date. The I-9 is kept in a separate I-9 binder or folder and is not filed in the general personnel file. The Administrator confirms with counsel whether Florida's E-Verify requirement for private employers applies to the agency's workforce size and documents the determination.

Before the employee's first client visit, the Administrator reviews the file against the checklist, signs and dates it, and informs the Scheduler that the employee may be assigned. No signature, no assignment.

Each month, the designee runs an expiration report and obtains renewals for CNA certification, CPR, in-service hours and rescreening 60 days before they expire. The Administrator reviews the report quarterly.
Personnel files are kept in a locked cabinet or in a secure electronic system with role-based access (REC-03). They must be produced to a surveyor during an unannounced survey (GOV-06; REC-04).

The agency retains personnel files for at least 6 years after separation, or longer if required by a contract or law. Form I-9 is kept for 3 years after hire or 1 year after separation, whichever is later. Employee medical records are kept as stated in PER-06.
Before survey, renewal or a payer audit, the Administrator performs a mock file audit of a sample of aide files, records the findings, and corrects deficiencies under the QAPI program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures each file is complete before first assignment, signs the File Completion Checklist, and keeps I-9 and medical files separate and secure.
Builds files, tracks expirations, verifies certifications and screening, and prepares the monthly expiration report.
Confirms aide competency and training documentation and medication-assistance training records, and signs competency evaluations.
Assigns only employees cleared by the Administrator.
Provides accurate documents and renewals before expiration and reports any change in certification or eligibility immediately.

documentation: Personnel file index and File Completion Checklist (signed and dated)
Aide training record or competency test result
CNA certification verification (Florida or other-state certificate)
Medication-assistance training record
CPR card
Annual in-service records
HIV/AIDS and dementia-related training records
Level 2 screening results and rescreening dates
Employment history verification and documented attempts
Written designation (administrator and alternate administrator)
Form I-9 (separate file) and E-Verify determination
Monthly expiration report

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Travel Time Compliance
policies.applies_to: All hourly employees including aides, CNAs, homemakers, companions and scheduling/office staff; Home Health Agency (non-skilled) and Homemaker and Companion registrant
federal: 29 CFR 552.109 (third-party employers may not claim the companionship or live-in exemptions)
policies.purpose: To ensure the agency pays all employees at least the Florida minimum wage, pays overtime, pays for all compensable time including travel between clients, classifies workers correctly, and carries workers' compensation coverage.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] classifies its caregivers as employees and pays them for all hours worked. Hourly pay is never below the Florida minimum wage set by Article X, section 24 of the Florida Constitution and s. 448.110, F.S., which is $14.00 per hour now and $15.00 per hour beginning September 30, 2026. Local governments may not set a higher private-sector minimum wage under s. 218.077, F.S., so the state rate applies in every county the agency serves. As a third-party employer, the agency may not claim the federal companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate applies to hours worked over 40 in a workweek (29 CFR 552.109). Time spent traveling between clients during the workday is paid working time. The agency carries workers' compensation coverage as required for employers with four or more employees under s. 440.02, F.S. The agency's practice is to carry coverage for all employees from the first day of hire. The agency does not treat caregivers as independent contractors; independent-contractor referral is a different business model (nurse registry) that this agency does not operate under this policy.

definitions.definition: All time an employee is required or permitted to work, including client visits, paperwork, required training, orientation, meetings and travel between clients during the workday.
A fixed, recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) beginning [DAY AND TIME OF WORKWEEK START].
The employee's hourly pay plus other required remuneration, used to calculate overtime.
An agency or other employer that is not the individual, family or household receiving services; it may not use the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions.

procedures: The Administrator sets the fixed workweek in writing and tells employees in the offer letter and handbook. The workweek is not changed to avoid overtime.

At hire, the Administrator classifies every caregiver as a non-exempt employee, issues the offer letter stating the hourly rate and duties, and reports the employee through payroll with required tax withholding. Caregivers are not placed on 1099 status.

Before each rate change and at least every year, the Administrator confirms that every hourly rate meets the Florida minimum wage. Before September 30, 2026, the Administrator updates payroll so no employee is paid under $15.00 per hour from that date, and documents the change. The agency does not rely on any local ordinance to set a different minimum.

Employees record time through the electronic visit verification and timekeeping system (SVC-09), from the start of the first client visit to the end of the last, plus all non-visit work time. Employees record time worked accurately and must not work off the clock.

Travel time between one client's home and the next client's home during the workday is recorded and paid as hours worked, whether or not the employee is driving. Travel from the employee's home to the first client and from the last client to home is treated as ordinary commuting, unless the employee first reports to the office or performs other work, in which case the time from that point is paid.
Orientation, competency evaluations, annual in-service, required meetings and office tasks are paid at the employee's regular rate and counted toward overtime.
The employee reviews and submits time each pay period. Supervisors review time for accuracy, missing punches and travel time before payroll processing, and payroll corrects errors before payday.

The Scheduler monitors hours daily. When any employee is projected to exceed 40 hours in the workweek, the Scheduler notifies the Administrator, who approves or reassigns the hours. Overtime that was worked is always paid, whether or not it was approved.

For any live-in or extended-shift assignment, the Administrator reviews the assignment with counsel or a payroll professional before it begins. Because the agency cannot claim the live-in exemption, all hours worked count and overtime applies. Any agreed meal or sleep period is deducted only if it meets legal conditions and is documented in writing.
Payroll pays overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours over 40 in the workweek, and calculates the regular rate to include non-discretionary bonuses and differentials.

The Administrator confirms workers' compensation coverage is in force before the first employee starts, keeps the policy and certificate on file, and posts the required workers' compensation notice. Employees report work injuries to the supervisor the same day; the supervisor completes the incident report (SAF-02; SAF-06) and starts the claim process.

Any employee may raise a pay question or concern with the Administrator or [PAYROLL CONTACT] without retaliation. The Administrator responds in writing within 10 business days and makes corrections, including back pay, as soon as an error is confirmed.

The Administrator reviews a sample of timesheets, payroll registers and travel records each quarter to look for unpaid travel time, off-the-clock work, rounding that favors the agency, and misclassification. Findings go to the QAPI committee (GOV-04) and the compliance process (GOV-05).
Payroll and time records are kept for at least the period in PER-07 and are available to the U.S. Department of Labor and the Florida Department of Revenue on request.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the budget so pay rates meet the minimum wage and overtime obligations, and receives quarterly compliance reports.
Ensures correct classification, rates, overtime, travel time pay and workers' compensation coverage, and investigates pay complaints.
Calculates pay, overtime and travel time accurately, updates rates by September 30, 2026, and keeps payroll records.
Builds schedules that account for travel time and monitors weekly hours to flag projected overtime.
Record all time accurately, report errors or missed pay promptly, and report injuries the same day.

documentation: Offer letters and classification records (non-exempt employee)
Written workweek definition
Time and attendance records and travel time records
Payroll registers showing hours, rates and overtime
Minimum wage rate review and 9/30/2026 rate update record
Workers' compensation policy, certificate and posted notice
Pay complaint log and responses
Quarterly timesheet audit results

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers and contracted staff who have contact with clients or their property; Home Health Agency (non-skilled) and Homemaker and Companion registrant
policies.purpose: To define the professional conduct expected of caregivers and to protect clients from exploitation, boundary violations and unauthorized services by setting clear rules and reporting duties.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires all staff to treat clients with dignity, to work only within their written assignment, and to maintain professional boundaries. Under Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l) and (p), F.A.C., an aide works only from a written assignment by a licensed health care professional and may not provide any personal health service that is not in the plan. Under Rule 59A-8.0095(12), staff must report unusual incidents, behavior changes and problems to the supervisor or case manager. Staff must not accept gifts or money, use client property, take or post client photos, or form dating or financial relationships with clients. Any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation must be reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873. Violations may result in discipline up to termination and, where the law requires, referral to authorities and licensing boards.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates the caregiver's helping role from personal, financial, romantic or social involvement with a client or the client's family.
The task list or plan of care assigned to the aide by the RN Supervisor or other licensed professional, which defines what the aide may do.
Improper use of a client's money, property or services for the benefit of someone other than the client.
Any event or change that is out of the ordinary for the client, such as a fall, injury, new confusion, refusal of care, missing property or a safety concern.

procedures: At hire, each employee receives a copy of this policy and signs an acknowledgment. The Administrator or designee files the acknowledgment in the personnel file, and the policy is reviewed at orientation and at annual in-service (PER-03).

Before each assignment, the RN Supervisor gives the aide a written assignment listing the tasks to be done. The aide reviews it with the supervisor and keeps a copy in the client's home or in the electronic system.

The aide performs only the tasks in the written assignment. If a client asks for a task that is not listed, such as a nursing or medical task, medication beyond the approved assistance, or a skilled procedure, the aide politely declines and calls the supervisor for direction. The supervisor decides whether to revise the assignment through the plan update process (SVC-03; SVC-04).

Staff must not accept money, gifts, loans, tips, bequests or favors from clients or family. If a client insists on giving a small token (such as food), the employee must tell the supervisor, who documents the event. Property and gift procedures are in CR-04.

Staff must not borrow from, lend to, or sell anything to a client. They must not use a client's belongings, vehicle, phone, accounts, cards or checks for personal purposes, or handle a client's finances except as written in the plan and as CR-04 allows.

Staff must not enter into romantic, sexual or dating relationships with clients. Personal, social or business relationships outside the care role must be disclosed to the supervisor before they begin.

Staff must not post or share client names, photographs, videos, addresses or details of care on social media, text groups or any public platform. Staff must not photograph clients or their homes except as the agency has authorized in writing. Privacy is addressed in CR-03.

Staff must not contact clients or their family off duty for personal reasons, share personal phone numbers or social media contacts, or provide unpaid services off the agency schedule. Client concerns outside scheduled hours are directed to the office or on-call line at [PHONE].

Staff must not work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs, bring visitors to a client's home, use tobacco in the client's home, or discuss their own personal problems, religion or politics in a way that pressures the client.

Staff must report unusual incidents, behavior changes and problems to the supervisor or case manager the same day, or immediately for emergencies. The supervisor records the report and follows up under SVC-10 and SAF-02.

Any employee who knows or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation of a client must immediately call the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 and notify the supervisor. The employee does not need permission or proof and does not investigate. SAF-01 governs the full process.

The Administrator investigates each suspected boundary violation promptly, interviews involved persons, protects the client from further risk (including reassignment of staff) and documents findings in a confidential file within 5 business days.

Confirmed violations lead to corrective action in line with the discipline policy, up to termination, and referral to law enforcement, AHCA or a licensing board where required. Retaliation against any employee or client who reports a concern is prohibited.
Staff are retrained on boundaries at each annual in-service, and the QAPI committee reviews boundary-related incidents and complaints each quarter (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Enforces this policy, investigates violations, applies corrective action and ensures reports are made to the Abuse Hotline and other authorities as needed.
Issues written assignments, directs aides on tasks outside the assignment, and receives and documents reports of incidents and behavior changes.
Work only within the assignment, maintain boundaries, decline gifts and personal favors, protect client privacy and report concerns and suspected abuse immediately.
Obtains and files signed acknowledgments and maintains discipline records.

documentation: Signed conduct and boundaries acknowledgment (personnel file)
Written assignments for each aide and client
Supervisor notes on reports of incidents and behavior changes
Gift or token disclosure log
Boundary investigation file and corrective action records
Abuse Hotline report confirmation numbers (kept per SAF-01)

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All client records; Home Health Agency (non-skilled) and Homemaker and Companion registrant
policies.purpose: To ensure each client has a complete, confidential, retrievable record that shows what services were agreed to, provided and supervised, and to set how long records are kept.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for every client it accepts. The record contains the written service agreement or service provision plan, services and assignments, signed and dated service notes, RN supervisory visit notes, required consents, evidence that required notices were delivered, and a termination summary where applicable (Rules 59A-8.020 and 59A-8.022(5), F.A.C.). For a registered homemaker and companion provider, the record also contains the items required by Rule 59A-8.025(8), F.A.C. Client records are confidential and are released only as described in CR-03 and REC-04. Records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys. Retention: the written agreement for an aide, homemaker or companion client without a treatment order serves as the service provision plan and must be kept for at least one year after termination (Rule 59A-8.020(3)). Because s. 400.491, F.S. controls retention and the agency has not confirmed the current subsection text, the agency keeps all client records for at least 6 years after the last date of service, which also meets the HIPAA 6-year documentation standard. The agency applies the longer period.

definitions.definition: The complete file, paper or electronic, containing all documents about a client's referral, acceptance, services, supervision and termination.
For aide, homemaker and companion clients without a treatment order, the signed written agreement that sets out the services to be provided.
A dated and signed record, written by the aide or caregiver for each visit, of the tasks done and any observations.
Able to be produced promptly in readable form for a surveyor during an unannounced survey, regardless of where it is stored.

procedures: At acceptance, the Intake Coordinator opens a record for the client and records the referral source, date of referral and acceptance decision (SVC-02).

The Intake Coordinator files the written agreement or service provision plan, signed and dated by an agency representative and the client or the client's representative. The client receives a copy, and the original is kept in the record (CR-06; SVC-03).

For each client, the record contains: the assessment, identification sheet, service plan or assignment, the services to be provided with their frequency and duration, signed and dated service notes, supervisory visit notes by the RN, and the termination summary (Rule 59A-8.022(5)).

For registered homemaker and companion clients, the record also contains the client's full legal name, address, phone number and age; the disability basis for service; the emergency contact, next of kin or guardian, and physician; the service agreement; the services with their duration and frequency; diet restrictions; food allergies; activity limitations; and any written termination notice (Rule 59A-8.025(8)).

The record contains the client's written consent for RN visits to the home and, where applicable, the client's informed written consent for medication assistance, both signed and dated (SVC-04; SVC-06).

The record contains proof that the complaint hotline, abuse hotline and Medicaid fraud hotline notices were given on or before the first day of service (CR-07), the special needs registry information and evacuation decision (SAF-05), and any advance directive information (CR-08).

Aides and caregivers complete a service note for every visit and sign and date it no later than the end of that visit (or in the electronic system by the end of the shift). The supervisor reviews notes at each supervisory visit and weekly for missing notes.

Entries are made in ink or in the approved electronic system. Corrections are made by a single line through the entry with date and initials, never by erasure or deletion. Electronic signatures must be authenticated, dated and protected from unauthorized access, and the agency must be able to reconstruct the record (REC-03; Rule 59A-8.022(6)).
Records are stored in locked cabinets or in a secure electronic system with role-based access. Only staff with a need to know may open a record.

No information is disclosed without the written consent of the client or guardian, except as the law allows. Record confidentiality is described in Rule 59A-8.022(2) and the agency's privacy policies (CR-03; REC-04).
On request of another agency or provider, with the client's consent, the Administrator transfers a copy of the record promptly and documents what was sent and when (REC-04).

On closure or termination of services, the RN Supervisor or Care Coordinator completes the termination summary and the Records Clerk closes the record within 14 days, noting the destruction-eligibility date (6 years after the last date of service).
Closed records are stored so that they can be retrieved during an unannounced survey. The agency keeps an index of closed records by client name, last service date and destruction-eligible date.

After the retention period, the Administrator approves destruction in writing. Paper is shredded and electronic files are securely erased, and a destruction log is kept. The agency does not destroy any record that is subject to a pending complaint, claim, audit, investigation or litigation hold.
On a change of ownership, records transfer to the new owner (GOV-07). On closure, records custody follows GOV-09.

The Administrator reviews a sample of active and closed records each quarter for completeness, signatures and retrievability, and reports findings to the QAPI committee (GOV-04). The Administrator confirms the current retention text of s. 400.491, F.S. at each annual policy review (GOV-03) and updates this policy if the period changes.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures records are complete, secure and retained as required, approves destruction and confirms current retention law annually.
Documents supervisory visits, reviews service notes and signs the termination summary.
Opens the record, obtains the signed agreement and consents, and files notices.
Maintains the filing system, closed-record index and destruction log, and retrieves records during surveys.
Complete signed, dated service notes for every visit and protect client information.

documentation: Client record index (checklist of required contents)
Signed written agreement or service provision plan
Referral, assessment and identification sheet
Signed and dated service notes
RN supervisory visit notes
Consents (RN home visits, medication assistance)
Notice delivery proof (complaint, abuse and Medicaid fraud hotlines)
Termination summary and written termination notice
Closed-record index and destruction log
Quarterly record audit results

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate administrator and compliance staff; Home Health Agency (non-skilled) and Homemaker and Companion registrant
policies.purpose: To make sure every report, notice and application the agency owes to AHCA, county emergency management offices, county health departments and the Florida Abuse Hotline is identified, assigned, filed on time and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] files all required reports and notices on time. Changes in the license application, insurance or bonds are reported to AHCA within 21 calendar days (s. 408.810(3), F.S.). Administrator and alternate administrator changes are reported to AHCA, with Level 2 screening of the new administrator (Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b), F.A.C.). Changes of address, counties served, or the opening or closing of a satellite office or drop-off site are filed on Form 3110-1011 (or 3110-1011OL) with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence (Rule 59A-8.003(8), F.A.C.). Changes in emergency-coordinator telephone numbers are reported to the county emergency management office and county health department of each county served (Rule 59A-8.027(4), F.A.C.). Abuse and exploitation are reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873. The Administrator keeps a compliance calendar and a reports log, and the alternate administrator covers the Administrator's reporting duties during absence.

definitions.definition: Any change in the information in the most recent license application, including ownership information, officers, administrator, address, counties served, insurance or bonds.
The Florida Agency for Health Care Administration, which licenses home health agencies and registers homemaker and companion providers.
A dated list of recurring filings and deadlines, such as renewals, CEMP review and rescreening, with a responsible person for each.
Every day, including weekends and holidays, counted from the day after the change occurs.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a compliance calendar with each recurring and event-driven filing, its deadline and its responsible person. The calendar is reviewed at each monthly management meeting.

Within 21 calendar days of any change in the information in the most recent license application, or in required insurance or bonds, the Administrator submits the change to AHCA in writing with supporting documents, and logs the date sent, the method and any AHCA confirmation (s. 408.810(3)). The Administrator does not wait for the deadline; reports are submitted as soon as the information is complete.

For a change of administrator or alternate administrator, the Governing Body names the successor in writing, and the Administrator submits the AHCA application forms required by Rule 59A-8.003(1) and notifies AHCA of the change under Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b). The new administrator completes Level 2 screening before serving, and the agency never operates without a qualified administrator on record (GOV-01; PER-02).

For a change of address, counties served, or opening or closing of a satellite office or drop-off site, the Administrator files Form 3110-1011 (or 3110-1011OL) with zoning approval and proof of the legal right to occupy the premises, as required by Rule 59A-8.003(8) (GOV-02; GOV-07). Services in a new county start only after AHCA approval.
For a change of ownership, the Administrator follows GOV-07 and files the required application and transfers client records to the new owner.

When an emergency coordinator's telephone number changes, the Emergency Coordinator reports the new number in writing to the county emergency management office and the county health department of every county served within 5 business days and files the confirmation (Rule 59A-8.027(4); SAF-04).

Each year, the Administrator reviews the CEMP against Form 3110-1022 and forwards the approved plan electronically to the contact designated by the Department of Health, as Rule 59A-8.027 requires. The Administrator keeps the transmission record (SAF-04).

Licensed agencies renew the license biennially, and renewal materials are prepared at least 90 days before expiration. The renewal application reports patient count and CEMP status, and the Administrator confirms the numbers against the client census before submitting. Registrants file their renewal at least 60 days before expiration (GOV-02; GOV-08).

Before the 30-day deadline to renew or discontinue, the Administrator follows GOV-09 for notice to AHCA and clients. Under s. 408.810(4), AHCA must have 30 days' notice before the agency discontinues operation.

Any staff member who knows or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation of a client reports it immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 and informs the Administrator, who confirms the report was made, records the confirmation number and follows SAF-01 and SAF-02.

Written reports to the Laboratory and In-Home Services Unit are sent to 2727 Mahan Drive, MS 32, Tallahassee, FL 32308, phone 850-412-4500, email Labstaff@ahca.myflorida.com. Registrants send their filings to the Long Term Care Services Unit, MS 33. The Administrator confirms the current mailing address and contact on the AHCA website before each filing.
The Administrator sends every filing by a trackable method or by email with a read receipt, and records in the reports log the date, content, method, recipient, tracking number and response received.
If no confirmation is received within 10 business days, the Administrator calls AHCA at 850-412-4500, documents the call and re-sends the filing if necessary.

The reports log and filed copies are kept for at least 6 years and are available to surveyors (REC-04). The QAPI committee reviews the log at least every quarter for late or missed filings and corrects the cause (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the compliance calendar, files all reports and notices on time, maintains the reports log and confirms receipt.
Covers filing duties during the Administrator's absence and knows where the calendar and log are kept.
Names administrators, approves ownership and address changes, and reviews quarterly the reports log.
Reports changes in emergency phone numbers to county offices and manages the annual CEMP review and submission.
Report suspected abuse immediately to the Abuse Hotline and tell the Administrator of any change that may need to be reported to the state.

documentation: Compliance calendar
Reports log with dates, methods and confirmations
Copies of AHCA submissions (Form 3110-1011 or 3110-1011OL, administrator change forms, insurance changes)
Zoning and right-to-occupy evidence
Emergency coordinator phone-change notices to county offices
CEMP annual review and electronic submission record
Renewal applications and fee payment receipts
Abuse Hotline report confirmation numbers

policies.title: Electronic Records, Electronic Signatures and Data Location
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff who create, sign, store or access client records, including office staff, RN supervisors, home health aides/CNAs, the Administrator and any contracted IT or software vendor. Applies to the Home Health Agency license limited to non-skilled services. Where [AGENCY NAME] also holds a homemaker and companion registration, it applies the same safeguards to those client files as good practice.
policies.purpose: To make sure that client records kept or signed electronically are authentic, dated, protected from unauthorized access, recoverable after a system failure, stored only in permitted locations and retrievable during an unannounced AHCA survey.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] may keep client records in hard copy, microfilm, computer disk or tape, or an electronic system, as long as every entry is authenticated and dated and the records can be retrieved during an unannounced survey (Rule 59A-8.022, F.A.C.). Authentication means a signature, written initials, or computer secure entry under a unique identifier of the primary author, who has reviewed and approved the entry. The agency maintains safeguards against unauthorized access and a written process to reconstruct records after a system breakdown. A plan of care or written order may be received by fax, and the original signature need not be on file. Any client data stored offsite or in the cloud is physically kept only in the continental United States, its territories or Canada. The licensee signs the affidavit required with the initial and renewal license application attesting compliance with s. 408.051(3), F.S. (s. 408.810, F.S.). Electronic safeguards are also designed to meet the HIPAA Security Rule administrative and technical safeguards (45 CFR 164.308 and 164.312).

definitions.definition: Any client record, note, plan of care, order, assessment or form created, signed, stored or transmitted in digital form.
A signature, written initials, or computer secure entry by a unique identifier of the primary author who has reviewed and approved the entry.
A user ID and credential assigned to one person only and never shared.
Client data held on servers or media not located in the agency office, including vendor-hosted software and backups.
The written procedure used to restore or rebuild client records after a system breakdown, data loss or corruption.
The staff member who performed the service or observation and is responsible for the content of the entry.

procedures: Before adopting any electronic records, scheduling, timekeeping or messaging system that will hold client information, the Administrator reviews it against this policy and approves it in writing. The approval is kept in the IT/vendor file.

The Administrator confirms in writing before contract signing, and again at each renewal, that all offsite, cloud and backup client data is physically stored only in the continental U.S., its territories or Canada. Vendor contracts must state the storage location and bar storage elsewhere.

The Administrator signs the affidavit of compliance with s. 408.051(3), F.S., with the initial and each renewal license application, only after verifying the data-location confirmation in step 2. A copy is kept in the licensure file (see GOV-02).
Each user receives a unique ID and password or other credential from the Administrator or designee. Sharing credentials is prohibited and is grounds for discipline under PER-09.

Access is role-based. Aides see only their assigned clients' plans and notes. RN supervisors and office clinical staff see the records of clients they supervise. Billing staff see only the information needed for billing. The Administrator approves access levels in writing.

Every electronic entry automatically captures the author's identity, date and time. If the system cannot do this, the author must type or write full name or initials, credential and date on each entry.
A staff member may authenticate only an entry they authored, or one they reviewed and approved as primary author. Staff may not sign or enter on behalf of another person.

Entries are made at the time of service or as soon as practicable afterward, and the date entered is always shown. A late entry is labeled as late and shows both the date of service and the date entered.
Corrections are made as an addendum or tracked amendment that preserves the original entry, author, date and time. Deleting or overwriting an original entry is prohibited.

A plan of care or written order may be transmitted by fax. The agency files the faxed copy in the record and does not need the original signature on file. Faxes are sent only to verified numbers with a cover sheet containing a confidentiality statement.

Workstations lock automatically after no more than [NUMBER] minutes of inactivity. Records are not left open on unattended screens. Staff may not save client information on personal devices unless the device is enrolled and approved under the Administrator's mobile device rules.

The Administrator reviews system user lists at least quarterly and immediately upon any termination, resignation or role change. Access for departing staff is disabled on or before their last day, and the date is documented.
The agency maintains encrypted, routinely tested backups of all electronic client records. Backup media and cloud copies follow the data-location requirements in step 2.

The Administrator keeps a written Record Reconstruction Plan that states who restores data, from which backup, in what order, and how paper copies, faxes, scheduling printouts and aide notes are used to rebuild missing records. The plan is tested at least annually and the test is documented.

If the system fails or is breached, staff notify the Administrator immediately. The Administrator activates the reconstruction plan, switches to paper forms so that service documentation continues, and logs the event, cause, records affected and recovery date. Any suspected unauthorized access is handled as a privacy incident under CR-03 and SAF-02.

When the system is restored, staff enter paper documentation promptly, labeled with the original date of service and date entered. The Administrator verifies completeness of reconstructed records before closing the event.

The Administrator ensures that records are retrievable during unannounced surveys by keeping a trained staff member available who can sign in, display and print any client record on request (see REC-04 and GOV-06). Staff are trained on this policy at orientation and when it changes (PER-03).

Electronic records are retained for the same period as paper records under REC-01. Before any system is retired or the vendor changed, the Administrator ensures the records are migrated or exported in readable form and verified.

responsibilities.duty: Approves systems and vendors, confirms U.S./territory/Canada data location, signs the s. 408.051(3) affidavit, assigns access, reviews user lists quarterly, owns the reconstruction plan and responds to breakdowns.
Performs these duties when the Administrator is unavailable.
Authenticates supervisory notes and plan reviews under the RN's own unique identifier and reviews entries before approving them.
Make timely, accurate entries under their own credentials, never share passwords and report system problems immediately.
Maintain faxed orders, scan paper records, monitor backups and assist with survey retrieval.
Provides contractually required security, backup and U.S./territory/Canada hosting, and supports recovery.

documentation: Written approval of each electronic system and vendor contract showing data location
Signed s. 408.051(3) affidavit copies with each initial and renewal application
User access list, access approvals and quarterly review log
Record Reconstruction Plan and annual test results
System breakdown and privacy incident logs
Staff training attendance records
Backup test logs

policies.title: Release of Information, Records Transfer and Surveyor Access
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff who handle, receive requests for, or disclose client records, including the Administrator, Alternate Administrator, RN Supervisors, office staff and aides. Applies to the Home Health Agency license limited to non-skilled services, and to client files kept for homemaker and companion services as good practice.
policies.purpose: To make sure client information is released only with proper written consent or as otherwise required by law, that copies are transferred to another agency promptly on request, that records move to a new owner correctly on a change of ownership, and that AHCA surveyors get timely access to records and a current client list.
policies.policy: Client information is confidential. [AGENCY NAME] does not disclose any information from a client's file without the written consent of the client or the client's guardian (Rule 59A-8.022, F.A.C.), except where disclosure is required or allowed by law and approved by the Administrator under CR-03. The signed written release is kept in the client record. On a client's request, the agency transfers a copy of the record to another agency. On a change of ownership, all client records held by the current licensee transfer to the applicant (Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C.). AHCA surveyors are given access to records, and a list of current clients within 2 hours of request. AHCA employees' use of client information is confidential. Requests for access by clients or their representatives, and disclosures generally, also follow the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR 164.502, 164.508 and 164.524).

definitions.definition: A signed and dated authorization from the client or guardian naming the person or organization to receive information, what information may be released, and the purpose, and stating an expiration and the right to revoke.
A court-appointed guardian, or another person with documented legal authority to act for the client.
Sending a copy of the client's record to another agency on the client's request.
A list of all clients currently receiving services from [AGENCY NAME] on the date of the surveyor's request.
A representative of the Agency for Health Care Administration conducting a licensure survey or investigation.

procedures: All requests for client information, whether verbal, by phone, fax, email, mail or in person, are routed to the Administrator or designee. Aides and other staff do not release information themselves.
Staff verify the requester's identity and authority before any release. For a requester claiming to be a client's representative, staff check the file for guardianship or legal authority documents.

Before releasing any information, staff check the client record for a valid signed and dated written release that covers the information requested and the named recipient. If none exists, staff obtain one by having the client or guardian sign the agency's Authorization for Release of Information form, or decline the request.
A release is not accepted if it is unsigned, undated, expired, revoked or does not name the recipient. The staff member returns it to the requester and explains what is needed.
The signed release is filed in the client record. Each disclosure is logged with date, recipient, information sent, method, purpose and staff initials.
Disclose only the minimum information needed for the stated purpose, except when the client is being transferred or the release covers the full record.

Disclosures required or permitted by law without consent, such as abuse reports or legal orders, are referred to the Administrator. The Administrator decides what may be released, consults legal counsel if needed, and documents the legal basis in the disclosure log (see CR-03 and SAF-01).

When a client asks for a copy of their own record, the Administrator or designee responds within the time allowed by 45 CFR 164.524 (30 days, with one permitted 30-day extension if the client is informed in writing), provides it in the form and format requested if readily producible, and logs the response.

When a client asks for a record transfer to another agency, the Administrator or designee obtains the client's signed request or release and sends a copy of the record to the receiving agency promptly. The agency does not delay a transfer because of any billing dispute.

Records are sent by a secure method, such as encrypted electronic transfer or tracked delivery. Faxes go only to a verified number with a confidentiality cover sheet. The agency keeps the original and documents the transfer date, method, recipient and staff member.

On a change of ownership, the Administrator works with the new owner to transfer all client records to the applicant, listing the records transferred, and documents the date of transfer. Client confidentiality is preserved during the transfer (see GOV-07).
On discontinuance of operation, client records are handled as described in GOV-09, and the Administrator maintains custody of the record transfer list.

When an AHCA surveyor arrives for a licensure survey or investigation, the first staff person notifies the Administrator or Alternate Administrator immediately. The Administrator or Alternate must be on premises within 1 hour of the surveyor's arrival (see GOV-06).

The Administrator or designee produces a current client list within 2 hours of the surveyor's request. The list is printed or exported from the client system and checked for accuracy before it is given to the surveyor.

Staff give the surveyor access to requested client records, in paper or on screen, and an authorized staff member sits with the surveyor to retrieve any record or electronic entry. Records must be retrievable during an unannounced survey (see REC-03).
Surveyors are given access to the records they need. The Administrator keeps a log of the records provided, and staff do not alter, remove or backdate any record during or after a survey.
Staff may not refuse a surveyor access to records or the client list. Concerns are raised with the Administrator, who handles any questions about the survey with AHCA.

The Administrator reviews the disclosure log at least quarterly for appropriateness, and unauthorized disclosures are handled as privacy incidents under CR-03 and SAF-02. Staff are trained on this policy at orientation and annually (PER-03).

responsibilities.duty: Approves or denies releases and legal disclosures, ensures timely transfers, oversees change-of-ownership record transfer, is on premises within 1 hour of a surveyor's arrival and reviews the disclosure log quarterly.
Performs these duties, including surveyor response, when the Administrator is unavailable.
Verify releases, log disclosures, prepare copies and transfers, and produce the current client list and records within 2 hours.
Helps the Administrator interpret clinical content in records and assists surveyors.

responsibilities.role: Home health aides/CNAs and all other staff
responsibilities.duty: Refer all requests to the Administrator or designee and never disclose client information without authorization.
Signs the release, specifies what and to whom information may be released, and may revoke the release in writing.

documentation: Signed and dated written releases in the client record
Disclosure log showing date, recipient, content, purpose and staff
Record transfer requests and transfer confirmations
Change-of-ownership record transfer list and receipt
Surveyor arrival log showing arrival time, Administrator arrival time, and time the client list was provided
Copy of the current client list provided to the surveyor
Log of records provided to surveyors
Training records on this policy
Privacy incident reports
